     so the issue's rule (the Host must equal the configured host and port) would refuse every tunnel on another
     port. The rule is on the **hostname**: `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]` or a name in
     `PI_CONSOLE_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, compared case-insensitively with a trailing dot stripped, any port; anything else is
     421. Rebinding is defeated by the hostname, which an attacker's DNS name never is, not by the port. The `Origin`
     check uses the Host the request carried, so it holds through any tunnel port. Measured on 2026-10-14 through a
     real tunnel to a unix socket (OpenSSH 9.9p2 on macOS to OpenSSH 9.2p1 in a Debian 12 container, `ssh -L
     9999:/home/op/run/console.sock`, the socket `srw-------` in a 0700 directory): Chrome 155 on `localhost:9999`
     signed in with a token and with a one-time link, made the same refusals as on a direct port, and a
     `host.docker.internal` Host through the tunnel was 421.
  3. **Another app on localhost is the same site.** A site ignores ports, so a page served from `localhost:3000` is
     same-site with the console, and its requests carry a `SameSite=Strict` cookie. That is why a write needs
     `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` exactly: `same-site` is refused, as are `cross-site` and `none`. Measured on
     2026-10-14 in Chrome 155 (headless, macOS), signed in to the console on `localhost`, then visiting a page on
     `localhost:3001`: its `text/plain` form POST and its `no-cors` fetch both reached the console carrying the
     session cookie and `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site`, and both were answered 403 and audited (`origin: ... Sec-Fetch-Site
     was same-site`); its JSON fetch never left the browser, because the preflight `OPTIONS` was answered 405 with no
     `Access-Control-*` header. Its credentialed GET of `/api/whoami` and its image GET also arrived with the cookie
     and were answered, but the page could read neither response. So `SameSite=Strict` does not stop a same-site
     page, as predicted; the write guards do, and every GET route must stay free of side effects. In the same run a
     name mapped to `127.0.0.1` (`evil.test`, Chrome's `--host-resolver-rules`) got 421 on every request, an inline
     script injected into a console page was blocked by the CSP (`script-src 'self'`), and neither the token nor the
     one-time code appeared in the request log or the audit log.
  4. **The operator's own pi session could mint a console token.** After a prompt injection, pi's `write` or `edit`
     tool could add an entry to the tokens file. The tokens file joins the pi extension's `guardedFiles()` (labelled
     "console tokens file"), the guard that already holds the envelope, the money files and the deployment's `.env`.
     The session's `bash` can still write it; that residual is the one `DES-ADMIN-VIA-PI-EXTENSION` already names
     for every guarded file, and the audit records each token the CLI adds. **The login codes are the same reach
     (AMENDED 2026-10-21, #708).** A file `<sha256(code)>.json` holding `{name, expiresAt}` in `console-login-codes/`
     beside the tokens file is a sign-in as the token it names, for whoever holds the code, and the session that wrote
     the file chose the code. So the login-codes directory joins the guarded files, as the tokens file is, as a
     DIRECTORY guard: a `write` or `edit` of the directory or of any path under it is refused, always judged by
     identity: where the directory exists, an existing ancestor of the target is its `(dev, ino)` (a symlink into it, a
     case variant, a `..` on the way); before the first code makes it, as `targetIdentity` judges a missing file, its
     nearest existing ancestor's `(dev, ino)` plus the folded segments below (review round 1 found a folded-path
     comparison bypassed through the macOS firmlink `/System/Volumes/Data/...`, a name that is no symlink; a bind mount
     or `/.vol` is the same shape). `envNamedFiles` adds it beside each reading of `PI_CONSOLE_TOKENS_FILE`. No key
     names the directory itself, so `GUARDED_ENV_KEYS` is unchanged. The residual is `bash` again, as for the tokens
     file. In depth, the consumer no longer trusts a file because it sits in the drop: a code file with any group or
     other permission bit, or another account's, is removed and refused (`mintLoginCode` writes 0600 as this
     account), and so is one whose `expiresAt` lies further ahead than a code lives (60 seconds, plus 5 of clock
     step). A drop another account can reach is refused with "remove the directory and make a new link", not
     "chmod 700": tightening the mode would make good any code planted while it was open.
  5. **A job could read the tokens file.** A local trigger whose `run.folder` contains the deployment folder mounts
     it into the job. The file holds sha256 hashes only, and a 256-bit random token cannot be recovered from its
     hash, so a read grants no login; it does name people and their roles. Doctor fails a tokens file inside
     any path a job container can see (a local trigger's `run.folder` or `run.skillsDir`, a `PI_DISPATCH_RUN_ROOTS` root, `PI_GLOBAL_PI_DIR`), the precedent of the allocation envelope, which the worker refuses to boot on when it
     lies inside any path a job container can see.
  6. **Two writers would fork the audit chain.** `serve` and a CLI command (`token add` while the console runs) both
     append, and two appends that read the same head would write two rows on one `prev`. No head is kept in memory:
     every append reads the head from the newest file and writes its row under a short append lock
     (`console-audit/.append.lock`, created exclusively with the writer's pid, removed in `finally`, taken over only
     when that pid is dead, never by age, so no skew between the filesystem's clock and the process's can let two
     writers in), so writers take turns; a test runs two processes appending 150 rows each and verifies one
     unbroken chain of 300. Separately, `serve` takes a single-instance lock,
     `<PI_LOGS_DIR>/console-audit/.console.lock`, created exclusively (`wx`) with its pid: a lock whose pid is alive
     refuses the second `serve` with a sentence naming it, a dead pid's lock is taken over, and the lock is released
     when the server closes. Two consoles on one deployment would hold two session stores and two rate limits, and an
     operator would not know which one revoked what.
- **Remote use**: the console terminates no TLS. Remote use is an SSH tunnel to the port
  (`ssh -L 4790:127.0.0.1:4790 host`) or to the socket (`ssh -L 4790:/path/console.sock host`), and the tunnel is the
  transport's security. A console on another host than the worker is allowed later, for reads: it needs only Valkey
  and the deployment folder, nothing in #640 depends on the host, and the audit's Valkey mirror (`console:audit`) is
  how such a console would read the log. Where run transcripts can be shown was `OQ-044`, resolved by #643: from
  the Valkey stream the worker publishes, so a console on any host shows any host's live run.
- **As a service** (2026-10-21, #708): `pi-dispatch service install --console` (worker/src/service.mjs) installs the
  console as the third component beside the worker and `--receiver` (mutually exclusive with it: every subcommand
  addresses one unit). One `execArgvFor(ctx)` gives every service manager the command (there were three copies, one
  per manager); the console's is `[<node>, <console.mjs>, "serve", "--deployment", <folder>]`, so it reads this
  folder's `.env` and tokens even where a manager's working directory were not honoured. One systemd template,
  `deploy/console.service` (mirrored, pinned in `TEMPLATE_PINS`, `RestartPreventExitStatus=2`, ordered after the
  network alone, inert in a user unit), and the launchd and nssm forms derived from the worker's as the receiver's
  are (label `com.pi-dispatch.console`, `console.{out,err}.log`, `AppExit 2 Exit`), so `serve`'s refusals (no
  operator token, the lock held, an unusable address) leave it stopped on every OS. A crash leaves the lock holding a
  dead pid, which the next start takes over; a pid since reused (or another account's, which reads as alive) keeps
  every start refusing, so the unit's comment, docs/console.md and doctor's fix say to remove the lock when its pid is
  not a console. **No `.env` in the console's environment** (round 1 review): the unit has no `EnvironmentFile=`,
  and the launchd and nssm forms set `PI_WRAPPER_NO_DOTENV=1`, which `worker-env-wrapper.sh` and `.cmd` test before
  their load (so no `.env` line can set it) and then neither source nor require `./.env`, `PI_ENV_SETUP` still run
  as configured. `serve --deployment` reads the file itself, only its own keys and only when no other account can
  change it; loaded whole, every worker secret would sit in the console's environment and each key would read as the
  shell's, which wins over the file and skips that check. **Paths are quoted per form**: each ExecStart word is a
  systemd word (`systemdWord`: bare when plain, else double-quoted with `\` and `"` escaped, `%` and `$` doubled), the
  `--env-setup` form keeps its old shape while every argv word is plain and otherwise passes the argv after the
  script (`exec "$$@"`), WorkingDirectory doubles `%`, every plist string has `&`, `<` and `>` escaped (no string
  lands in an attribute, so quotes stay literal), and `readUnitSeam` undoes both, for the folder and the setup path;
  a control character (anywhere) and surrounding whitespace (Linux) are refused before anything renders, and `%`
  joins the Linux `--env-setup` refusals. A `--` in a macOS folder is NOT refused: plutil accepts it in the template's
  comments, and with `>` escaped a path cannot write `-->`. Worker and receiver renders of plain paths are
  byte-identical to before. Two consequences for existing installs, both deliberate: a unit whose paths hold a
  character outside the bare class (`[A-Za-z0-9_@+=:,./-]`, or on macOS `&`, `<`, `>`) renders different bytes after
  an upgrade and a re-render (`--force`), both forms being valid and the old one having split or expanded that path,
  so a path that was broken now works; and on Windows `"`, `%`, `&`, `|`, `<`, `>` and `^` are now refused in ANY
  command word, the worker's node and cli paths included, where `nssm` and the wrapper's `%*` would already have
  split or rewritten them. Scope as the receiver's: user by default,
  `--system` staged and printed. No cross-scope refusal: a second console is refused by `serve`'s own lock, not
  destructive. The entry is `import.meta.resolve("@edgehero/pi-dispatch-admin/dist/console.mjs")` when that file
  exists (the admin package is not a worker dependency and has no `exports` map, and `import.meta.resolve` does not
  check existence, measured on node 23.5), else the REAL path of the `pi-dispatch-console` on this shell's PATH, taken
  only when it ends in `dist/console.mjs` beside a package.json naming the admin package (a pnpm or Volta shim is
  refused: `node <shim>` would crash at every start); the PATH lookup does not run on Windows, which the refusal
  says. With neither, render and install refuse, saying to install the admin package where this worker is
  installed. `--drain` is refused for the receiver and the console (it drains the worker's queue). `install` also refuses when the tokens file the
  SERVICE would read (PI_CONSOLE_TOKENS_FILE from the deployment `.env`, through the reader the console uses) holds no
  operator token or cannot be used, since the unit would then exit 2 on its first start and stay stopped; `up`
  judges the same file through the same helper (`consoleTokensPathFor`). `doctor`
  (`consoleServiceChecks`) names an installed console unit for this folder (`installedUnitPaths` gains the console;
  `readUnitSeam`'s WorkingDirectory; `nssm status pi-dispatch-console` on Windows) and whether the console answers
  (worker/src/console-probe.mjs, imported lazily: one `GET /healthz`, `Host: 127.0.0.1`, 1 s, to the loopback address
  as written, `127.0.0.1` or `::1` for an any-address bind, or the unix socket; port 0, a non-loopback address and an
  unparseable value answer "unknown" and contact nothing): ✗ when a unit is installed and nothing answers, ⚠ when
  there is no unit and nothing runs, ✓ otherwise, and no line at all while `PI_CONSOLE_LISTEN` is one `serve` refuses
  (its own ✗ says so). The worker exports the probe as `@edgehero/pi-dispatch/console-probe`, and the admin's
  `/dispatch console` (#708 part 1) imports it, so there is one rule. `up` prints `pi-dispatch service install
  --console` among its next steps once an operator token exists and no console unit is installed for the folder. Rejected: a Quadlet unit (the console runs no container); a unit naming the bare
  `pi-dispatch-console` (a service manager's PATH is not the shell's, and launchd's cannot see an nvm or Homebrew
  prefix); refusing at `render` over the token (it writes nothing, and the unit is right once a token exists);
  judging liveness by the lock's pid (an alive pid is not an answering listener, and a recycled pid is not the
  console); and probing a configured non-loopback address (a read-only command would send a request across a
  network).
- **The cookie's attributes**: `Secure` and the `__Host-` prefix are set only if Chrome, Firefox and Safari keep such
  a cookie on `http://127.0.0.1` and `http://localhost`, where the console is served without TLS; a browser that
  drops it would make login silently fail. Measured on 2026-10-14 with a server setting three cookies over plain
  http: Chrome 155 (headless, macOS 15.7) sent back all three on both hosts, but WebKit (a `WKWebView`, the engine of
  Safari 18.6) sent back only the plain one and dropped both the `Secure` cookie and the `__Host-` one. So the
  cookie is the plain name `pdc_session`, `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/`, without `Secure`: with it, a Safari
  operator could never log in. Firefox is unmeasured. Nothing is lost on the wire, where the cookie never leaves the
  loopback hop or the tunnel.
- **The screens** (issue #641, `REQ-OPERATOR-CONSOLE-SCREENS`): eight read pages, each an exact path with a bounded
  query string, so the route table stays a table of exact paths and the #640 tests that iterate it cover every page
  without a hand list. `/` is the overview, `/runs` the run history (the run filters and a `before` cursor), `/run?id=`
  one run, `/parked` the parked inbox, `/insights?range=7d|30d|mtd` the spend and insights sections (since
  2026-10-18 also `whatif=` with `flow=`, and `paths=full`), `/fleet` the
  queues, hosts, schedules and failed jobs, `/config` the configuration and `/audit` the audit log (operator only).
  Beside them: `GET /api/state` (`INT-CONSOLE-STATE-API`), `GET /api/events?page=` (`INT-CONSOLE-EVENT-STREAM`) and
  `GET /static/console.css`. The page set is one frozen table, `PAGES` in `admin/src/console/pages.mjs`
  (`name -> {path, auth, live, title}`), from which the routes are built.
  - **A page is a list of panels.** Each panel is a pure renderer from the page's data to an escaped fragment
    (`admin/src/console/panels.mjs`), placed in `<section id="p-<name>" data-panel>`, and the SAME renderer serves
    the first load and every live update, so a live page cannot drift from a reloaded one. `loadPageData` is the
    only function a page reads through, and it calls the fleet reader's `snapshot()` at most once per call.
  - **Every query is judged before anything is read.** `parsePageQuery` bounds and charset-checks every value and
    refuses a bad one by field name, never echoing it. The run filters are `parseRunFilter`
    (`admin/src/run-filter.mjs`, pure): ten fields (`repo`, `kind`, `flow`, `trigger`, `project`, `host`, `outcome`,
    `reason`, `model`, and `q`, a case-insensitive substring of the target), each matched exactly but `q`, each
    with the charset of the shape the worker writes into that record field, so a refusal can never hide a run that
    exists; a field given twice is refused rather than one copy winning, and a value is never trimmed into one that
    passes. The `model` rule is one exported pattern, `RUN_MODEL_RE` (issue #668): the record's bare model id with
    one optional leading `@` or `~`, as the priced catalog's `@cf/...` and `~anthropic/...` ids carry and the usage
    ledger's allowlist (`MODEL_REF_PATTERN`) admits. `/api/run`'s `safeRunOf` and the what-if form's model part use the
    same pattern rather than a copy each: the copy `/api/run` held duplicated the filter's (both refused those ids),
    and the what-if's own extension admitted a leading `@` or `~` followed by anything other than a letter or digit
    (`provider/@`, `provider/~`, `@.x`, `~/x`; none of them a priced id) that the filter did not.
  - **No inline style.** The CSP's `style-src 'self'` blocks an inline `<style>` and every `style=` attribute, so the
    stylesheet is a served file (`admin/src/console/style.mjs`, `CONSOLE_CSS`) built from the insights page's own CSS
    (`INSIGHTS_CSS`, now exported), the panel's theme tokens (`PAGE_THEME`) and the console's layout rules; the one
    `style=` the insights renderers carried became a class. The insights section renderers are exported and reused,
    never copied, and their tooltips are `data-tip` indexes the served script reads.
- **One fleet reader, so there is no second read model**: the panel's snapshot code (`createDashboardDeps` and
  `fetchSnapshot` in `dashboard.ts`, which held one client and a pool of failFast queues for the 1 s tick) moved into
  `read-model.mjs` as `createFleetReader(paths, seams)`, returning `{snapshot, runsPage, runById, pause, resume,
  cancelActive, dispose}`. The panel and the console each build one, so the two surfaces read the deployment the same
  way; copying the panel's loop would have made the console a third reader. It was moved, not rewritten: the
  panel's existing tests pass unchanged, and that is the proof the move is a move. The read model's other readers
  open and close a client per call (a queue per fleet queue plus a SCAN for the queue state), which is right for a
  command and far too heavy for a 1 s poll. The snapshot gained, for both surfaces: every active job (`active`,
  `{jobId, queue, startedAt, host}`, never a job's `.data`, beside the old `activeJobId`), counts per queue
  (`queueCounts`) beside the summed ones, `parked`, and `failures24h` (folded from a wide window of the newest 1000
  merged runs, read at most once per 15 s; `failures24hFloor` says the window did not reach back a day, so the count
  is a floor). New readers, each over an injected client:
  - `readRunsPage`: one page of the merged history, newest first, at most 100 runs. **The cursor is a score, not an
    offset**: `before` is the instant of the last run shown, so a run that lands while an operator pages lands above
    every cursor already handed out and moves nothing, where an offset would shift every later page and show a run
    twice; a page never ends inside a group of runs that share one instant. It filters after fetching, in batches,
    and stops after examining 2000 records (`RUNS_PAGE_EXAMINE_MAX`), answering `truncated` with a `next` that
    resumes exactly where it stopped, so a filter that matches nothing costs a bounded read per request. The mirror
    side is `readMirroredPage` (a `ZREVRANGEBYSCORE` and one `MGET`), and `readMirroredRuns` gains `prune: false`:
    the mirror read the panel uses prunes stale members, which is right for one reader and wrong for a page any
    viewer can load, since a page read must not write. The local side is an index of this host's records held
    across requests and re-read at most every 15 s. Merged by the worker's `mergeRuns`, as the panel merges.
  - `readRunById`: this host's file first, because the file is the record, then the mirror's by-id read; an id
    outside the charset the worker mints is refused before any path or key is built from it.
  - `readParkedRuns`: a parked run is `outcome: "completed"` with `reason: "awaiting-input"` (`REQ-AWAIT-INPUT`).
    Nothing records that one was answered, so `answered` is derived: a later run on the same kind and target, since
    an answer is a new delivery on that issue. The chain count is the session store's `resume-chain` counter at the
    re-derived key (`DES-SESSION-KEY-IS-DERIVED-NOT-INDEXED`) when `PI_SESSIONS_DIR` is on the console's host, else
    unknown, never 0 for a store this host cannot see. A pull request's key needs its head ref, which the record does
    not carry, so its count is unknown too.
  - `secretProfileNames` (names only, never a resolver path or a value), and the worker's `readConsoleAudit` (newest
    rows first, a position cursor, at most 500 rows a call, bounded memory over the chunked month files; a line that
    is not a row comes back as `{broken, file, line}` in its place rather than being skipped, because an audit screen
    that drops a damaged line hides what `audit verify` exists to name).
  - `forgeLinkOf(record, env)`: **derived from the deployment's environment, never guessed.** GitHub on
    `github.com`, as the panel always built it; GitLab, Forgejo and Azure on the deployment's own instance URL
    (`GITLAB_URL`, `FORGEJO_URL`, `AZURE_ORG_URL`, then the job-container names in `FORGES[kind].hostVars`), http
    or https only, with no credentials, query or fragment. Null on a control byte, a repository outside its forge's
    charset, a `.` or `..` segment, a separator the forge never writes, or no instance URL: a link an operator
    clicks to the wrong host is worse than none.
- **Insights in the console**: `assembleInsights` and its sub-assemblers moved from `index.ts` into the pi-free
  `admin/src/insights-assembly.mjs`, which takes the pricing as a parameter. `index.ts` imports it and its behaviour
  and tests are unchanged. The console passes the worker's real pricing (`@edgehero/pi-dispatch/pricing`), so its
  bundle carries `pi-ai` for the price table, as the extension bundle already did, but never the pi runtime: the
  console is not a pi session and must not load one. An assembly walks run records, so the console caches it 30 s
  per (range, paths).
  - **The one analytics surface** (2026-10-18, insights move to the console): the static insights export is gone
    (`REQ-INSIGHTS-HTML-EXPORT`, retired) with its page chrome (the whole-page builder and the page around the
    sections; the section renderers and the stylesheet the console uses stay), the graph dir and its setting, and
    the browser spawn; `/dispatch insights` prints this page's URL (`DES-ADMIN-VIA-PI-EXTENSION`). The page took
    what the file alone had. Its default window is 30d, the file's, because the topology is pinned at a 30-day
    record window and one page's two halves should describe the same period; its header states both windows and the
    retention and scan cap sentence. **The what-if** is a GET form on the page
    (`/insights?whatif=<provider>/<model>&flow=<flow>`), a read for either role and not an action, so it takes no
    ticket and writes no audit row: it answers the same estimate the command did (`whatIfFlow`, the median per-run
    quad re-priced at the target over the flow's ledgered runs, else the seeded band `unmeasured (OQ-002)`) in a
    what-if panel. Its record scan is the 92-day scan ceiling, as the command's was, so one request is bounded, and
    the answer is cached 30 s per (model, flow, scan window), at most 64 answers, so a viewer reloading it, or
    many viewers, cost one scan. An unknown model is answered with the closest priced ids (at most three, a
    contains filter over the priced catalog) and scans nothing, so a typo costs no read. `whatif` and `flow` go
    together, and both are charset checked by `parsePageQuery` (the model like the runs filter's model rule, which
    may also start with `@` or `~` as the priced catalog's Cloudflare and OpenRouter alias ids do, with a provider
    before the first `/`, the flow the skill name rule; every id the pinned catalog prices passes, a test walks it) before anything is read; a `<datalist>` offers
    the priced ids and the window's flows. **`paths=full`** draws full local folder paths in the topology's group
    labels and the budget split's problem text for the operator role alone; a viewer's request still draws
    basenames and the page says full paths are for operators, because a path names the host's layout and the
    viewer role is the one handed to people who should not learn it. **The interactive topology** (pan, zoom, chip
    tooltips, label fitting and a breakdown row's click highlighting its chip through `data-node`) is part of the
    one served script, `/static/console.js`. Its per-node tooltip and neighbour data reach the script as a hidden
    escaped list in the page, escaped by the one template, never as an inline
    script element or embedded JSON, because the CSP's `script-src 'self'` refuses every inline script, and a
    `<script type="application/json">` block would also be a second escaping context (a forged `</script>` in a
    flow name) beside the one HTML escaping every other value already goes through. The zero external requests
    property the file held is now this page's, held by the CSP and the page tests.
- **The live hub** (`admin/src/console/live.mjs`): live updates are server-rendered panels over Server-Sent Events
  (`INT-CONSOLE-EVENT-STREAM`). One poll loop in the console process, every second (the panel's cadence), and only
  while at least one stream is open, so a console nobody watches reads nothing and N open tabs cost Valkey one poll,
  not N; a runs view, whose filters make every distinct query its own read, reloads at most every 5 seconds. Each tick
  it loads each distinct page and query once, renders that page's panels, digests each, and writes
  only the panels whose digest changed, as `event: panel` with a rising `id`. A stream opens with every panel of its
  page, unless its `Last-Event-ID` is the current id, in which case it missed nothing; a `: ping` comment every 15 s
  keeps a tunnel or proxy from closing an idle stream; a client whose unsent buffer passes 2 MiB is ended, and its
  browser reconnects to a fresh snapshot, rather than the process that holds operator power buffering for a reader
  that does not read. The browser swaps the `innerHTML` of the matching `data-panel` element with that
  server-escaped fragment; the CSP still forbids inline script, so a swapped fragment can run nothing.
- **The stream lifecycle**: #640 judged the session on each request, and a stream is one request that does not end,
  so #640 had no way to end a stream when its session died. Now each tick the hub re-judges every stream's session
  with `sessions.peek(id, file)`, which runs every check `get` runs (idle, absolute, generation, token hash and role)
  but neither moves `lastSeen` nor deletes. Re-judging with `get` would have kept an idle session alive for as long
  as a tab stayed open, turning `PI_CONSOLE_IDLE_MINUTES` into "never" for anyone who leaves the console open: **an
  open stream never extends a session; only a request does.** A stream whose session fails gets `event: end` and is
  closed, so revoke, rotate, a role change, `sessions end-all`, the idle limit and the absolute limit end it within a
  tick, and logout ends that session's streams at once through the hub's registry (`endSession`). Slots: at most
  `PI_CONSOLE_MAX_STREAMS` streams per token across all its sessions (default 4; per session would let one token
  multiply its budget by signing in again), and at most 32 in the whole process with 8 kept for the operator role,
  so streams can never take more than half of the 64 connections and a viewer token cannot lock operators out of
  live pages; a stream over either cap is refused 429, and `res.on("close")` releases its slot. A stream outlives
  `requestTimeout` and `headersTimeout`, which bound how long a request takes to arrive, not how long its response
  runs. An event stream carries the security headers of every response, plus `Content-Type: text/event-stream`,
  `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`.
- **The role and run-text rule** (`REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY` (l)): run records are PII-free by construction
  (`INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT`), so every page shows them to both roles. The strings in them a hostile party can
  shape (`jobId`, `target`, `parentJobId`) are scrubbed and escaped by the one template, like every value. The one
  free text the screens read is BullMQ's `failedReason`, the worker's own throw message, de-payloaded at its sources
  and belt-scrubbed (`DES-ADMIN-VIA-PI-EXTENSION`, the FAILED surface): it reaches a page only for the operator role,
  only in a detail view, never in a list, and never in a viewer's `/api/state`. The audit page is operator only,
  because its rows name people, session digests and refused hostnames. A test walks every page as a viewer with
  hostile fixture values. #641 showed no transcript and no `.log`; #643 adds the live transcript on the run page,
  under the same rule (below). No page shows a `.log`.
- **The live transcript** (issue #643, `REQ-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT`, `DES-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`): the run page
  (`/run?id=`) gains a "Live transcript" section for the operator role. A viewer sees a sentence that transcripts are
  shown to operators only, and nothing of the stream. A run with no stream says it is not published, expired or not
  started yet, since the stream cannot tell those apart. While the stream exists, the section opens a second kind of
  event stream, `GET /api/transcript?id=<jobId>` (`INT-CONSOLE-EVENT-STREAM`), operator only, implemented in
  `live.mjs` beside the hub as a second subscription type:
  - it shares the hub's slots (per token, global, the operator reserve), the per-tick session re-judging with
    `peek` (`event: end` when the session ends) and the 2 MiB cut;
  - each tick it reads `transcriptSince` from the stream's own cursor, non-blocking `XRANGE` on the fleet reader's
    client, and writes each entry as `event: entry` with `id:` the stream entry id and data `{html}`;
  - the html is rendered on the server by the one template: a header (kind, tool, an error marker, the time in UTC)
    and the text in an escaped `<pre>`, tool-call arguments and tool results in `<details>`, no markdown and no
    inline style;
  - a reconnect's `Last-Event-ID`, validated as a stream id (`TRANSCRIPT_ID_RE`), resumes after that entry;
  - once the reader has read the `end` entry it sends `event: done` with the outcome and closes.
  The served script appends each entry's html to the `[data-transcript]` element, follows the bottom unless the
  operator scrolled up, and shows live, ended or not live. The section is `<section id="transcript">`, deliberately not a
  `data-panel`, so the hub never renders or swaps it; the script's states are live, reconnecting, ended with the
  outcome, and not live, and with no stream the page says "No live transcript: not published (PI_LIVE_TRANSCRIPTS=0),
  expired, or not started yet." A run page whose run has no record yet but a live stream answers 200, since a running
  job has no record until it ends. The run-text rule holds unchanged: transcript text reaches the
  operator role alone, escaped after the control scrub, only on the run page, never in a list, never in
  `/api/state` and never in a hub panel.
- **Run progress** (issue #644, `REQ-RUN-PROGRESS`, `DES-RUN-PROGRESS`, `INT-RUN-PROGRESS-KEY`):
  - The active table (`activeTable`, shared by the overview and the fleet page) gains a "Progress" column for both
    roles: integers and the running call's `LIVE_TOOL_RE`-checked tool name only (the turn, the steps, the failed
    steps, the running tool and its age, the phase's index of its count), rendered escaped, from the fleet snapshot's
    integer `progress` (`activeProgressOf`, `INT-CONSOLE-STATE-API`), so no list and no viewer sees model text. An
    ENDED snapshot shows `-` (the job is active, so the key is an earlier attempt's), and a STALE one (`progressStaleFor`:
    not ended and `updatedAt` older than 180 s, `PROGRESS_STALE_MS`) ends with "no update for 4 min; the worker may be
    gone" and gives its running tool no age (`progressText`).
  - The run page gains a "Progress" panel, its first panel (`p-progress`): counters, running tools, recent steps and
    the phase's integers ("Phase 2 of 4: 3 of 10 done") for both roles; the phase names, the current phase with a
    `<progress>` bar (an element, since the CSP forbids inline style) and the note for the operator role alone,
    escaped after the control scrub (the run-text rule above: phase names and notes are model text). A finished run
    shows its record's `progress`, re-checked with the worker's `recordedProgress`, labelled "Sum of step durations"
    (`toolMs`, steps of a parallel batch overlapping) and "Longest interrupted step"; the live resume prior is "Earlier
    runs of this session". With no key the panel says "No live progress: not published (PI_RUN_PROGRESS=0), expired, or
    no step has been recorded yet." A STALE snapshot leads with "Stale: no update for 4 min; the worker may be gone."
    and its open steps read as open at the last update, never as running with an age the console's clock keeps
    growing. A retried job keeps its id, so a record and a key can be different attempts, judged by time: a key that
    started after the record's `endedAt` is the running attempt's and is shown live under "An earlier attempt of this
    run ended (`<outcome>`); this is the attempt after it."; the key's phase names join the record only when the key has
    ended and started inside the record's attempt (no earlier than the record's `startedAt`, no later than its
    `endedAt`; a key that started earlier is an earlier attempt's, left in place by an attempt refused before its
    container); a record whose start or end cannot be read pairs with no key. A #645 recovery is not a retry (issue
    #662): it has its own job id and writes the RUN's key, so the page reads the key by the run id (`readRunProgress`:
    the record's `recoveryOf`, else the queue job's `data.recoveryOf`, else the page's id) and a recovery's own page
    shows its live progress; an attempt whose record says `recovery-enqueued` pairs with no key and shows its own
    record's `progress` under "This run continues as `<recovery job>`." (the NEWEST recovery job of the run after it,
    in any state, `laterJobOfRun`: with `.r1` and `.r2` both held the base names `.r2`, where the run lives now; "a recovery job" once the queue no longer holds it). Rejected: telling the attempts
    apart by time as for a retry, since the recovery's key started after the attempt's record ended and would read as
    "the attempt after it", a different job's live steps on this attempt's page. The fleet snapshot's active rows read
    a recovery's key by its run id too, and the `/dispatch` panel follows the same rule (its ACTIVE row's phase name
    through `progressOfRun`; RUN_DETAIL of a `recovery-enqueued` record shows its own progress and "continues as" the
    recovery job, read once on entry like the sandbox state).
  - **The run page is now a LIVE page**: the hub re-renders its panels by digest (no new route), and its data is read
    at most once every 2 s (`LIVE_DEFAULTS.pageMinMs.run`). An operator's run tab therefore holds two streams, the
    hub's and the transcript's, against the token's `PI_CONSOLE_MAX_STREAMS` (default 4). A running job with no
    record yet answers 200 when it has a progress snapshot or a transcript.
- **Steering a running job** (issue #646 part 3, `REQ-STEER-RUNNING-JOB`, `INT-STEER-INBOX-CONTRACT`):
  - Two entries join the action table: `steer` (paid) and `steer-withdraw` (free), each a preview and a confirm
    through the generic pipeline below. Their planners, `planSteer` and `planSteerWithdraw`, sit in `job-actions.mjs`
    beside the parked answer's, and their funnels, `enqueueSteer` and `withdrawSteerMessage`, call the worker's own
    inbox module (`@edgehero/pi-dispatch/steer-inbox`), so the console refuses with the CLI's sentences. The job is
    found across the fleet's queues and must be active and steer-armed, and its run open (`run:steer:open:<runId>`,
    the run id the base run's for a recovery); the text is bounded by the inbox's own rule and the whole entry checked
    by `normalizeSteerEntry` at the preview, so nothing the push would refuse for its size reaches the confirm. The
    message id is minted at the preview, so the ticket binds one message and a replayed push can only be `dup`. A run
    that closed or went quiet after the preview refuses the confirm (`closed`, `gone`): never accepted and silently
    unseen. Both rows name the message: `target` is `<job id>#<message id>` (`steerAuditTarget`), never the text.
  - **A recovered run** (review round 1): a #645 recovery keeps the run id under a new job id, so the base run's page
    shows a job that failed while its run goes on. `activeJobOfRun` tries the run's recovery ids (`recoveryJobId`,
    `RECOVERY_CAP` down to 1, then the run id itself) for the ACTIVE one; the panel then says "its run continues as"
    that job, linked, and keeps the forms, and `planSteer` sends through that job, naming it in the preview.
  - **Paid, with no new reserve.** The run already holds its reservation, and its turn, dollar and token caps bind
    the turns a message causes, so the preview says it spends from that reservation and shows no reserve figure, and
    the row carries none. The text is shown escaped to the operator who typed it, in the preview alone; the row holds
    its sha256 as `afterDigest`. A withdraw's preview and answer name the state met: `queued` is guaranteed, `written`
    best effort.
  - **The run page's Inbox panel** (`p-inbox`, after Progress): for a steer-armed job, its messages from
    `readJobInbox` (the fleet reader's `inbox(jobId)`, off its held client, the registry read afresh) WITHOUT TEXT for
    both roles, the run's status (takes messages; not open, the three causes named; or no longer running), and for
    the operator role on a console that is not read-only a steer form and a follow-up form, drawn only while the job
    is active and its run open, and a Withdraw button on each queued or written message whose id is well formed. A
    job that is not steer-armed draws nothing, its empty section hidden by `section[data-panel]:empty`, so every other
    run page reads as before. The page is live, so the hub re-renders the panel by digest and a message's state moves
    without a reload; a form in use is not swapped.
  - The fleet snapshot's active rows gain `steer` and `inbox` for a steer-armed job (`INT-CONSOLE-STATE-API`), read
    for at most 16 of them per tick (`STEER_INBOX_ROWS_MAX`), one MULTI each beside the progress MGET, which reads
    the state hash's `m:<id>` metadata and never the list, so no message text moves on a tick (review round 1); of a Job's
    `.data` it reads `steer` and `recoveryOf` and nothing else, and the run id never leaves the reader. An unarmed row
    carries neither field.
  - **Rejected**: listing a message's text, even to an operator (the inbox is a channel into one run, and a list is
    drawn for every tab and every viewer: the operator who typed it sees it in the preview, and the run's transcript
    shows what the agent received); a reserve per message (the run's caps already bound what a message causes, and a
    second hold would refuse a message to a run that can afford it); and a model-callable steer tool
    (`DES-ADMIN-VIA-PI-EXTENSION`: a message enters a running agent's context, so its sender is a person at an operator
    surface, never the operator's own model).
- **Run chat** (issue #647 part 1, `REQ-TERMINAL-CHAT`, `DES-TERMINAL-CHAT`):
  - **The run page's Chat panel** (`p-chat`, between Progress and Inbox, `runChat`): the chat the run can have now,
    from `chatFactsOf` (the fleet reader's `jobStatus`, `readJobStatus`: any job's BullMQ state across the fleet's
    queues and its active #645 recovery, steer-armed or not; the newer-run search, a runs-page read, only for a parked
    record, `searchNewer: "parked"`) through `chatModeOf`. It composes what the page already has, never a second copy
    of an action: live shows a link to the transcript section (or the recovery job) and the steer and follow-up forms,
    which MOVE here from the Inbox panel while the panel draws them (`chatDrawsSteer`, the Inbox panel's own rule:
    an operator on a writable console, an active or continued steer-armed job, an open inbox), so the page never holds
    two forms for one action; reply shows `parkedAnswerForm`, the one form the parked inbox draws; fork shows
    `pi-dispatch chat <id>` to copy (shown, never run, like the sandbox command), or why the record names no session
    (no `run.resume`; a pull request, `sessionKeyOfRecord` null). Live and reply show the command too. A viewer gets the
    state and a refusal's sentence, never a form or a command; a read-only console draws no form; a fleet with no
    job-state reader draws nothing. Since review round 1: reply shows the form only where `planParkedAnswer` would plan
    the answer (`parkedAnswerRefusalOf` through `parkedAnswerCheck`) and the planner's sentence otherwise; a park being
    answered and a queued recovery link the job that holds the run; a live run whose inbox could not be read says so
    rather than "not steer-armed". The parked rows of the snapshot carry `answering` (the shared pending-answer scan,
    `DES-TERMINAL-CHAT`), which `/parked` draws as its Answer column (no form for a park being answered) and the
    overview leaves out of its waiting count; `/api/state`'s parked projection does not carry it. Review round 2: the
    rows also carry the scan's own answer (`pendingScan`), and `/parked` draws a form only where `parkedVerdictOf`
    says reply, the verdict the Chat panel reaches through `chatModeOf`, so an unknown park has no form on either screen.
  - **`GET /api/run`** (`run-api.mjs`, `INT-CONSOLE-STATE-API`): one run by `?id=` or `?url=` with its state, mode,
    active job, steer status, transcript existence, progress integers, forge link and newer run on its target, every
    field rebuilt by its shape (`safeRunOf`). A viewer's route, because nothing in it is free text, job data, transcript
    text or a session key. `?url=` resolves through `forgeTargetOf`, the INVERSE of `forgeLinkOf`, held to it by a
    round-trip test on every forge, read only on the deployment's own instance URLs and github.com; beside
    `forgeLinkOf`'s own shapes it accepts the request URLs a person copies, GitHub's `/pull/<n>` and Forgejo's
    `/pulls/<n>`. An Azure work item names no repository, so its runs decide, and several repositories are a 409
    with candidates, never a guess. A queue that cannot be read is a 503: a mode judged on half the facts is worse
    than none.
  - **`format=json` on `/api/transcript`** (`INT-CONSOLE-EVENT-STREAM`): the terminal's structured entry, on the same
    route, role and slots; the hub renders once per format per tick. The browser keeps the server-rendered HTML (the
    rejection of browser-side rendering below stands).
  - **`/api/state`'s parked rows** gain `jobId`, so a script or the terminal can open or answer one without a second
    lookup.
- **Doctor results** (AMENDED 2026-10-21, #712 PR C, `DES-DOCTOR-RESULTS-PUBLISHED`, `INT-DOCTOR-RESULTS-KEY`): the
  fleet reader's snapshot carries `doctor`, each host's last published doctor run, read for the index's hosts and the
  live ones at most every 15 s (a host publishes daily, so a per-tick MGET would be load for nothing), never pruning
  from the console. The Fleet page's Doctor panel (`fleetDoctor`, after Hosts) draws per host the age, the counts and
  the failing and warning checks with their fix, failing first; a result older than two of its host's own intervals is
  flagged stale, a live host that published nothing is named, and an unreadable read is a warning, so no absence reads
  as health. The configuration page's "does not load" sentences (`doctorReason`, for the triggers, pause-windows,
  scoped-limits and projects files and the settings overlay) quote the newest published check by its NAMED id and name
  its host and age; without one they keep "run pi-dispatch doctor for the reason". The labels are doctor's sentences
  after the publisher's redaction (no path, no URL beyond its host, no secret-named value or known token shape, no file
  text a parse error quoted), so they are shown to both roles and
  escaped like every value; they are not run text. The `/dispatch` panel's HOSTS view gives each host the same lines
  (`doctorLines`), fitted to its width. Not on `/api/state`.
- **Wiring**: `serve` builds one `createFleetReader` on the deployment's Valkey, with `installPanelValkeyContext`
  applied as the panel applies it so TLS and auth deployments connect the same way, and with `PI_SESSIONS_DIR` when
  it is set; it builds the insights cache, the audit reader and the hub, passes them to `createConsoleServer` as named
  dependencies, and disposes all of them on stop. `SERVER_LIMITS` is overridable for tests only.
- **The action table** (issue #642, `REQ-OPERATOR-CONSOLE-ACTIONS`): every write the console makes is one entry of a
  frozen table, `ACTIONS` in `admin/src/console/actions.mjs`, shaped `{name, kind, paid, bulk, preview(body, ctx),
  apply(entry, ctx)}`. `preview` answers `{refusal}`, `{unchanged}` or `{summary, diffHtml, expect, payload,
  targets, reserve}`, and writes nothing; `apply` answers `{ok, results?}` or `{invalid}`. The routes are generated
  from it, two per entry (a preview and a confirm, `auth: "operator"`, `write: true`; `POST /api/act/<name>/preview`
  and `/api/act/<name>/confirm`), so the #640 dispatcher puts every
  guard in front of every action and the tests that iterate the route table cover every action without a hand list.
  The refusal tests that once hit the one pause-windows route by hand loop over the table. The pause-windows write
  of #640 is the table's first entry; its old routes, `/api/pause-windows/preview` and `/confirm`,
  stay as aliases of the same handler and ticket (a whole-list replace, kind `pause-windows-set`). The table holds no
  validation of its own: each `preview` calls a planner in `admin/src/write-plans.mjs` or `admin/src/job-actions.mjs`
  and each `apply` calls a read-model funnel, the same pair the `/dispatch` TUI and the pi extension's tools call, so
  a value the panel refuses is refused here in the panel's own words.
- **The generic pipeline**: one preview handler and one confirm handler serve every entry, so the ticket, the
  re-check, the audit row and the compensating row are written once.
  1. The preview runs the entry's `preview` and, on a plan, issues a ticket holding `{action, payload, expect,
     targets, reserve, beforeDigest, afterDigest}`: what the confirm will do, the snapshots it was built from, the
     jobs it will touch, and the reserve the page showed. It answers the summary, the diff (a `SafeHtml` fragment
     built by the one template, swapped by the served script into `[data-preview]` alone) and the ticket.
  2. The confirm redeems the ticket (single use, this session, this action, 5 minutes, unchanged from #640), appends
     the `ok` audit row with `kind`, the digests, `reserve` and `count`, then runs `apply`. A refusal or a throw
     appends a compensating `failed` row under the same ticket digest. An append that fails refuses the write
     before `apply` runs.
  3. `apply` hands the ticket's `expect` to the funnel, so a confirm applies exactly what was previewed or refuses
     with "changed after this change was built from it" (a file) or "it changed since the preview" (a job), and the
     page answers 409 and asks for a fresh preview.
  4. After an `apply` that landed, the hub is poked (`hub.tick()`) so every open live page shows the change.
  The served script handles every `form[data-action]` the same way: preview, show, confirm, reload. No inline
  handler, and the CSP is unchanged.
- **The action groups**, each a funnel that already existed or one #642 added beside the others in the read model
  (`job-actions.mjs`, re-exported by `read-model.mjs`, so the read model stays the admin's one data access surface):
  - **Runs and jobs**: cancel an active job (`requestCancel` through the fleet reader's `cancelActive`, the CLI's
    channel, with `REQ-OPERATOR-JOB-CANCEL`'s named refusal when no worker acknowledges); cancel a held job
    (`cancelHeldJob`); retry a failed job and remove a failed job (`retryFailedJob`, `removeFailedJob`: BullMQ's
    own `job.retry()` and `job.remove()`, only on a job still `failed` with the previewed `attemptsMade` and
    `finishedOn`); re-run a finished run (`planRerun`, `enqueueRerun`, paid); answer a parked run
    (`planParkedAnswer`, `enqueueParkedAnswer`, paid); since issue #646, send a message into a running job
    (`planSteer`, `enqueueSteer`, paid with no new reserve) and withdraw one (`planSteerWithdraw`,
    `withdrawSteerMessage`).
  - **Fleet**: pause and resume the whole fleet (`killSwitchPlan` and `killSwitchSet`, the tools' funnel, so a
    resume across two disagreeing Valkeys is refused here as it is everywhere); pause and resume one queue
    (`setQueuePausedOne`, which refuses a name the fleet does not drain rather than creating a paused queue
    nothing reads).
  - **Configuration**: triggers add, edit and delete (`writeTriggers`); settings set and unset (`writeSettings`);
    secret profile names, a name and its resolver path added or removed, never a value (AMENDED 2026-10-20, #704: and
    bundle resolvers, a name, its resolver path and its format, `secret-bundle-add` and `secret-bundle-remove`,
    `DES-PROJECT-SECRET-BUNDLES`); pause windows; scoped
    limits; projects; the envelope; priorities (shows the plan before it applies); revert an allocation. Each is
    the matching `plan*` of `write-plans.mjs` for the preview and the panel's funnel for the write, which now
    takes `expect` on every file it writes.
  - **Bulk**: retry every failed job, remove every failed job (either filtered by queue or by repository), and
    cancel every held job.
  The audit `kind` of each is the panel's where the panel already writes the same thing (`trigger-add`,
  `setting-set`, `cancel-held`, `fleet-pause`, ...), and the console adds `queue-pause`, `queue-resume`,
  `failed-retry`, `failed-remove`, `failed-retry-all`, `failed-remove-all`, `held-cancel-all`, `run-rerun`,
  `parked-answer`, `steer` (which the panel writes too, issue #646) and `steer-withdraw`. The action names are the
  kinds' own spellings for the configuration actions (`trigger-add`, `setting-set`,
  `limit-edit`, ...) and `cancel-active`, `cancel-held`, `cancel-all-held`, `retry-failed`, `remove-failed`,
  `retry-all-failed`, `remove-all-failed`, `fleet-pause`, `fleet-resume`, `queue-pause`, `queue-resume`, `rerun`,
  `parked-answer`, `steer` and `steer-withdraw` for the rest.
- **Paid actions and the reserve**: a re-run and an answer to a parked run start a paid job, so their preview shows
  what the worker will hold before the operator confirms, and the ticket and the audit row carry it (`reserve`, in
  micro-dollars). The figure is `estimateReserve` (`worker/src/reserve-estimate.mjs`, the worker export
  `./reserve-estimate`), which imports the worker's own rule rather than restating it: one job-count slot in each
  window that applies, and in dollars the per-job cap `effectiveCostCapMicros(trigger maxCostUsd, deployment
  maxCostUsd)` (the smaller of the two, each counted only when set, the deployment's resolved `overlay > env`), or 0
  for a job that cannot spend (`zeroRatedFor`, the processor's own zero-rated test, moved beside it so the estimate
  and the reserve judge one rule), or "no cap" when neither is set. Without the worker's endpoint snapshot the
  estimate judges a job not zero-rated, so it can name a larger figure than the worker holds and never a smaller one.
  `CONST-BUDGET-BEFORE-TOKENS` is unchanged: the worker still reserves at pickup, after every free gate, and the
  page only says beforehand what that reserve will be. A retry also runs a job again, through every pre-spend gate, so
  it is paid too: its preview reads the failed job's data and shows the same estimate, and a bulk retry shows each
  job's and the sum; a job whose data cannot be read shows "reserve unknown", never $0. Resuming the fleet or a queue
  is marked paid as well, since it releases jobs that will reserve.
- **Answering a parked run** (`REQ-AWAIT-INPUT`'s console source): a comment posted as the deployment is dropped by
  the receiver's self-guard, so the console cannot answer by commenting as the bot. It enqueues the reply job
  itself:
  - The job is the one the RECEIVER builds for a phrase-free reply on that forge's issue, field for field: the
    parked run's `repo`, `projectId`, `azure` and issue target from its retained BullMQ job (kept 31 days), the
    comment trigger's run fields as the triggers file says now, `resume: true`, `parkedReply: true`, `matched`
    naming the comment trigger, and the answer in `trigger.comment.body`, which the prompt fences as data below the
    delimiter like any comment (`CONST-ISSUE-TEXT-IS-DATA`). Four fields differ, by design: a fresh delivery id
    (`console-<16 hex>`, never a forge's, so its job id cannot collide with one), the sender (`{id: null}`), the
    GitHub author association (`OWNER`: the operator is the deployment's own authority, `CONST-TRIGGER-AUTHOR-GATE`'s
    operator clause), and `console: {by: <token name>}` at job level, never inside `trigger`, so the agent's
    `event.json` does not carry it. A test builds the receiver's reply and the console's for the same issue and
    compares them field for field.
  - The text is scrubbed (line endings made `\n`, other C0 and C1 controls, DEL, and the bidi overrides and isolates
    removed, the line and paragraph separators made `\n`) and refused, never cut, when empty or above 8 KiB
    (`worker/src/console-answer.mjs`, export `./console-answer`, the one rule both sides use).
  - Refused by name before any ticket: a run that is not parked, one already answered (a later run on the same kind
    and target), a pull request's park (its reply needs the head branch, so it keeps the phrase on the forge),
    expired data, and a comment trigger the receiver would not route a reply through (absent, a command, or without
    `run.resume`).
  - The worker's gates apply as for any reply: the `not-parked` check first, then the budget reserve. A job that
    passed `not-parked` and carries `console.by` posts ONE trail comment through the existing `comment` adapter,
    once every pre-spend gate and reserve has passed, just before the container starts, so the issue never reads
    "answered" above a refusal that then dropped the answer, and still before the provider is called:
    "Answered from the operator console by <name>:" followed by the text as a blockquote, every `@` followed by a
    zero-width space so the answer cannot mention a person or team under the deployment's identity (an answer from the
    panel's `/dispatch chat`, signed with the reserved `panel`, reads "Answered from an operator's /dispatch panel:"
    instead, and the planner refuses a console token of that name, issue #647 part 2). The name needs
    no escaping: `enqueueForgeJob` refuses a `console.by` outside the token-name charset (lowercase letters, digits,
    dot, dash, underscore, at most 32), and the worker posts nothing for one that is not. The trail is posted as the
    deployment's identity, which the receiver's self-guard drops as `self`, so it never starts a job. A later
    pre-spend refusal (a budget cap, a missing session store) still follows the trail, which then reads as an answer
    that was given and not acted on, the same as a forge reply refused there.
  - The trail is posted AT MOST ONCE per job: before posting, the worker sets `console:trail:<jobId>` with NX and a
    31-day expiry, and only the attempt that set it posts, so an infrastructure retry or a console retry of the
    answer's job never quotes the answer twice; on a Valkey error the trail is skipped and logged
    (`console_trail_skipped`) rather than risk a second one. The quoted text escapes `&`, `<` and `>` as entities
    before the mention neutraliser runs, so an HTML comment or tag cannot hide part of the answer on the forge and an
    entity cannot spell a mention; the answer scrub also removes every bidi mark (U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A to
    U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069) and turns U+2028, U+2029 and carriage returns into newlines.
  - The audit row records the parked run's job id and the sha256 of the answer, never the text.
- **Re-run sources, per kind** (`planRerun`): a run record cannot rebuild a forge job (it holds no payload text, by
  construction), so each kind is rebuilt from the source that can:
  - LOCAL (`/dispatch run`, `pi-dispatch run`, a chained child): the retained job's folder, flow and task, queued as
    `/dispatch run` queues them (`enqueueLocalJobReporting`, this host's queue), after the same folder rule (a
    repository root with a commit and no uncommitted changes), re-checked at the confirm. A local job's data is kept
    24 hours after it completes and 7 days after it fails.
  - CRON (`repeat:` and `manual:` ids): the trigger as the triggers file says NOW, fired once by hand
    (`enqueueTriggerRunReporting`, `pi-dispatch run --trigger`'s path and refusals, through the worker's
    `loadSchedules`, export `./schedules`).
  - FORGE: the issue (repo, project, target, trigger context) from the retained job's data, but the RUN FIELDS
    (flow, model, models, cost cap, secret profile, image, backend, packages, mcp) from the trigger at the retained
    `matched.index` as the triggers file says NOW, built by the same `runFieldsOf` the parked answer uses, and listed
    in the preview. That trigger must still be the same forge and type, still list the matched label or action, and
    run the same flow (a comment's flow override only while the file still routes that flow, never through a command
    trigger); otherwise the re-run is refused, "the trigger that started this run changed or is gone; start it again
    from the forge". Replaying the retained fields was rejected: a trigger deleted or narrowed to stop a secret
    profile, an image or a cost would have come back for 31 days, and a shifted index would have pointed the worker's
    trigger-skew check at another trigger. A fresh `console-<hex>` delivery id makes the job id new; it is routed as
    the receiver routes it (`jobNeeds`/`routeForgeJob`), and carries no `console` field (a re-run is not an answer).
  Refused by name: expired data, a `/command` run (a command runs only from its reviewed trigger), an answer to a
  parked run (answer again from the inbox instead), a cron trigger gone from the file or served by another host.
  The forge job's 10-minute semantic window, and the local and cron minute windows, can still take the re-run as a
  duplicate; only the enqueue can tell, and it says so by name with nothing queued.
- **Bulk actions**: the preview lists every affected job, at most 100 (`BULK_MAX`), with each failed job's
  `attemptsMade` and `finishedOn`, and the ticket binds that exact list and each job's state; a set larger than 100
  shows the first 100 and says how many more matched. The confirm acts per job, re-checking each one, so a job
  retried, removed or failed again since the preview is refused alone and the rest go on, and the answer reports per
  job. The audit has one row per job (`target` the job id), each with `count` the list's size and the one ticket
  digest, so a reader can group a bulk action and see each job's outcome.
- **One audit chain**: the TUI's writes and the extension's tools' writes land in the same log as the console's,
  as actor `{name: <os login>, role: "panel", session: null}`, in the deployment's `PI_LOGS_DIR/console-audit/`.
  `auditedWrite` (`admin/src/audited-write.mjs`) applies the console's rule to them: the `ok` row before the write,
  a compensating `failed` row with the same ticket after a refusal or a throw, and a write whose row cannot be
  appended does not happen. The log's append lock already lets several writers on one host take turns, so the
  console, its CLI and a pi session append to one chain. Before #642 only allocation writes were recorded outside
  the console, so the log could say what a browser changed and nothing about the same change made from a terminal.
- **The sandbox, shown and not run**: the run detail page shows `pi-dispatch sandbox <jobId>` for the operator to
  copy and run on the host. Reopening a sandbox is `docker run -it` with the operator's terminal inherited
  (`worker/src/sandbox.mjs`), which a separate process cannot hand to a browser; `REQ-RESURRECTABLE-SANDBOX`'s
  surfaces are unchanged. **AMENDED 2026-10-21 (#712)**: shown only for a run whose venue has a sandbox shell
  (`serves.sandboxShell`, held to `SANDBOX_LAUNCHERS` by the worker's test; a record naming no venue is a `local` run,
  `UNATTRIBUTED_BACKEND`), and otherwise the reason the panel's sandbox pane gives in the same words
  (`sandboxShellRefusal`: "not reopenable (openshell has no sandbox shell)"). It printed the command on every run, and on
  `openshell` the command can only refuse.
- **Every sentence is true for the run's venue (AMENDED 2026-10-21, #712).** What a venue serves and why a run went
  without a feature are said from the worker's own tables, never restated per surface: `admin/src/read-model.mjs`
  holds `STEER_SKIPPED_TEXT` (the record's `steerSkipped`), `LIVE_SKIPPED_TEXT` (its new `liveSkipped`,

  `CUSTODY_TEXT` (`CREDENTIAL_CUSTODY`), each bolted to its worker enum by `admin/test/venue-words.test.mjs` so a new

  a resolver whose real path on this host is outside it, before the confirm: the resolver resolved with `realpathSync` and compared with the roots AS WRITTEN, exactly as the worker compares (it never resolves a root), the refusal adding "or write the root as its real path" where a root's own real path would hold it. A path this host cannot resolve (an error with a `code`) is admitted with a Note in the confirm, even when it is outside the roots as written, deliberately: its real path is unknown here; any other error is rethrown. Judged on the console's or the panel's host, which may not be the worker's. Residual: the `realpathSync` calls are synchronous on the UI path (one per root at most), accepted for a dialog-time check. A trigger add or edit arming
  `run.recover` on a venue that does not serve it, named or `PI_BACKENDS[0]`, is refused before the confirm
  (`recoverVenueRefusal`); `PI_BACKENDS` there is the surface's own environment (pi's, or the console's), as
  `backendRefusal` reads it, not the deployment's `.env` (`OQ-038`), so a surface started without it judges against
  `local`. The Venues view is #712's second part.
- **The Venues view (AMENDED 2026-10-21, #712, part B).** Which venues each host runs, and what each venue declares,

  Each venue in `BACKENDS`' order: the hosts that bless it and default to it, every property as the table's own

  - **Rejected: a live check per venue from the console** (spawning `docker`, `podman` or `openshell` on the console's

  - **Rejected: a Venues column on the HOSTS view's lines.** That view's lines are slots, budget and history, already

- **A run's OpenShell facts and the secret profiles (AMENDED 2026-10-21, #712 part D).** The run page shows a run's

  (`resolverRootsStatus`, the one rule the add's pre-confirm `resolverRootsJudgement` now reads too: the resolver's

  run ended before a container, and the record cannot say whether the resolve ran); and the live hosts whose registry

  console names-only, the panel's sections are names-only by the bundles section's precedent, and the view's rows
  carry none, so neither surface can. `/dispatch secrets list` prints the same facts under the declared tables it

  50) and no registry, and says so. Residual: the view calls `realpathSync` once per overlay profile per snapshot (a

  LEXICALLY against the roots, where this view and both adds use the realpath, so the two views can disagree about a

  a run read by its id, only the host count in a list, and the counts) and `secretsProfile` (a name
  `dispatch_triggers` already shows), rebuilt or dropped whole (`modelRunRecord`); no model-callable read gains a
  resolver path, and the profiles view is not on one. **Code evidence**: admin/src/read-model.mjs ->
  secretProfilesView, resolverRootsStatus, realPathOrNull, SECRET_RESOLVE_REASONS, PROFILE_SOURCE_TEXT,
  PROFILE_ROOTS_TEXT, secretProfileFacts, renderSecretProfilesView, recordOpenshell, recordSecretsProfile, hostRowOf,
  modelRunRecord; admin/src/write-plans.mjs -> resolverRootsJudgement; admin/src/console/panels.mjs -> profileUse,
  openshellRows; admin/src/dashboard.ts -> profilesSection, renderRunDetail; admin/src/secrets-command.ts;
  admin/test/secret-profiles-view.test.mjs.
- **The panel as a second minter, and the return path (ADDED 2026-10-21, #708).** `/dispatch console --link` (the
  operator-typed subcommand of `DES-ADMIN-VIA-PI-EXTENSION`) mints a one-time login code in the panel's own process,
  for an operator token of the tokens file, through the same `mintLoginCode` and drop as `pi-dispatch-console link`.
  The trust is the same: the panel runs as the deployment account, which can read the tokens file and write the drop
  anyway. Three rules differ from the CLI's, each the stricter one:
  - **audit, then mint**: a `login-code` row with actor role `panel` and the token's name as target is appended
    before the code exists, and no code is made when it cannot be appended (the panel's rule, `audited-write.mjs`); a
    mint that is then refused gets a `failed` row under the same `ticket`. The CLI appends after its change, as every
    CLI change does;
  - **only where it counts**: only for a console the probe found running (a code lives 60 seconds; "unknown" is
    refused too), only in pi's terminal UI (`ctx.mode` exactly `"tui"`, so a pi too old to say refuses: in RPC mode
    `hasUI` is true but a notice goes to the RPC client, another program), and only into the drop beside the tokens file `guardedFiles()` guards (one helper,
    `consoleTokensPathFor`, gives both), so a session whose deployment the panel cannot see never mints where its own
    `write` could have planted a code;
  - **opened without its code on a command line**: the browser is handed a 0600 redirect page in a fresh 0700
    temporary directory (`open-link.mjs`, `location.replace` with the fragment kept, removed after 60 seconds or by
    the next run), because an opener's argv is readable by every local account while it runs;
  - **operators only**: a viewer token is refused with the CLI command to use instead, and with several operator
    tokens the operator picks one in a select; none is refused with the `token add` hint;
  - **notify only**: the link is shown in the operator's notice, never sent into model context, and the token is never
    printed, read from or written to `.env`. With no pi UI the command refuses before it probes or mints.
  The link may name the page to land on, after the code in the fragment: `login/code#<code>&next=/runs`. Since the
  link's text is anyone's to write, `next` is held to this console's own pages twice: the server's `POST /login/code`
  answers `next` judged by `returnPathOf` (at most 1024 characters, a single leading `/`, no `//`, no backslash, no
  control byte, no fragment, this origin, a `PAGES` path, and a query that page's own `parsePageQuery` accepts; else
  `/`), and the script navigates there only when that answer is also one of `PAGES`' paths, else `/`. `/login` and
  `/login/code` are not pages, so a link cannot loop back into sign-in. The code stays in the fragment, so neither it
  nor `next` reaches a request line, a log or a `Referer`; `next` travels in the JSON body of the sign-in POST, beside
  the code. **Code evidence**: admin/src/console-command.mjs -> consoleCommand; admin/src/console/pages.mjs ->
  returnPathOf; admin/src/console/server.mjs -> postLoginCode, startSession; admin/src/console/script.mjs (the
  login-code branch, `ownPage`); admin/test/console-command.test.mjs, admin/test/console-login-next.test.mjs.
- **Rejected**:
  - **`next` in a query string, or a redirect from the server** (2026-10-21, #708). A query string reaches the request
    log and the history (the reason the code is in the fragment), and a server-side redirect to a path the request
    named is the open-redirect shape itself. The page path rides in the fragment and comes back as a JSON answer the
    script checks again.
  - **Keeping a second, offline insights renderer beside the console** (2026-10-18). From #641 the console served
    the insights sections while the extension still wrote the static insights export, with its own page chrome, its
    own inline script, its own reload loop and its own window default (30d against the console's 7d); the two
    drifted (the full paths opt in and the interactive topology existed only in the file, the what-if only as a
    command beside it, and a
    screenshot of one could not be checked against the other). An offline copy also kept a second security posture
    to argue (a file anyone can forward, with a flag that put host paths in it) beside the console's roles. One
    served page under one CSP and one role model is the narrower surface; the file and everything only it needed
    (the graph dir, the opener, `--no-open`, `--full-paths`, the reload) went.
  - **Mounting the console on the receiver.** Still rejected, for the reason `DES-PANEL-SEPARATE-FROM-RECEIVER`
    recorded and `DES-ADMIN-VIA-PI-EXTENSION` kept: the receiver binds `0.0.0.0` and faces the forge, so any admin
    surface on it is published to the internet, and one crash in the console would take webhook ingress with it.
  - **A web framework or a build step.** A framework puts its dependency tree in the process that holds operator
    power, for a handful of routes, and a client build step puts a bundler between the reviewed source and what the
    browser runs. Server-rendered template literals with one escaping helper keep the escaping in one place, which
    is the property that matters when the page renders hostile text.
  - **TLS in the process.** TLS is the tunnel's job. A loopback listener with a self-signed certificate adds key
    material to protect, trains the operator to click through a warning, and protects a hop that never leaves the
    machine.
  - **One shared token** (the issue's first proposal). The audit could not name a person, and revoking one person's
    access would rotate everyone's.
  - **bcrypt or another KDF for the stored hashes.** A KDF slows the guessing of a secret a person chose. A console
    token is 256 random bits, which no guessing reaches, so sha256 is enough; a KDF would only add a per-login cost
    that a local attacker could use to slow the operator's logins further. The code says so beside the hash, so it
    is not later "fixed".
  - **A cookie with `Secure` or the `__Host-` prefix.** WebKit drops both on plain-http loopback (measured, see the
    cookie's attributes above), so either would lock Safari operators out.
  - **The token in a URL** (`?token=`, or a token login link). A query string reaches the server's request log, the
    browser's history and a `Referer`. The one-time link instead carries a code in the **fragment**, which the browser
    never sends to the server; a same-origin script POSTs it, it is single use, lives 60 seconds, and is never the
    token.
  - **A Valkey stream as the audit record** (the issue's proposal). A capped stream forgets by design and a Valkey
    flush loses it. The month file is the record and Valkey a best-effort mirror, as the allocation audit and
    `alloc:log` already are.
  - **JSON over the stream and rendering in the browser** (issue #641). The escaping would move into browser code,
    a second escaper beside the template, and the property that matters when a page shows hostile text is that
    there is one. Server-rendered panels keep it, and the same renderer serves a reload. The transcript's JSON format
    (issue #647) does not reopen this: it serves the terminal, which is not an HTML sink and scrubs for its own
    (`DES-TERMINAL-CHAT`), and the browser still gets only server-rendered HTML.
  - **A single-page app or a client framework for the live pages** (issue #641). The live updates did not change
    the reason a framework and a build step were rejected above; a panel swap needs a few lines of served script.
  - **Each browser polling** (Valkey through an API, or the page reloading itself). N open tabs would be N pollers
    and N times the reads on the deployment's Valkey; one poll in the console fans out to every stream.
  - **WebSockets** (issue #641). The updates go one way, and SSE is enough: it is a plain GET through the same
    dispatcher and guards as every page, and the browser reconnects with `Last-Event-ID` by itself. A WebSocket
    needs upgrade handling on the trusted process, a second framing to parse, and an origin check of its own (a
    WebSocket handshake is not held by the same-origin policy), all for a channel the console would never read
    from.
  - **A terminal in the browser** (issue #642), to reopen a sandbox from the page. Reopening is an interactive
    `docker run -it` with the operator's terminal inherited; carrying it to a browser means a pty and a duplex
    channel in the process that holds operator power, an interactive root-adjacent shell one stolen session away
    from anyone, and the WebSocket handling rejected above. The page shows the one command instead, and the operator
    runs it where they already have a shell.
  - **Committing configuration to git** (issue #642). A config edit lands in the files the TUI writes (the triggers
    file, the overlay, the money files) and nothing else. Committing would give the console process a git identity
    and a repository to write, turn a confirmed file write into a second, separately failing step, and take a
    decision that belongs to the operator's own review workflow; the files stay diffable for whoever commits them.
  - **Posting the answer as the bot from the console process** (issue #642, the issue's own first question). A
    comment posted as the deployment is dropped by the receiver's self-guard (`sender.id === selfId`), so it could
    never resume the run, and it would put a forge credential in the console. The console enqueues the reply job and
    the worker, which already holds the forge identity, posts the trail just before the container starts.
  - **Re-running from the run record** (issue #642). The record is PII-free by construction: it holds no issue text,
    no comment and no folder, so it cannot rebuild a forge job or a local one, and adding those fields would break
    the property `INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT` exists for. The retained BullMQ job holds them for a bounded time
    (31 days for a forge job), and a re-run past that is refused by name.
- **Residuals**, stated rather than implied (each is a "What is NOT defended" entry in `SECURITY.md`): root on the
  host reads and writes everything the console does; a compromised operator browser or machine acts with the
  operator's session; a compromised tunnel endpoint is the operator; a local user can spend the global login rate limit
  and slow the operator's own login, and can hold the 64 connections open (each cut ten seconds after it stops short
  of a full request, so the holder must keep reconnecting) to keep the operator out while it lasts; on Docker Desktop
  a job on a TCP listen is such a user, and unix-socket mode removes both paths; and the operator session's `bash`
  can write the tokens file and, since #708 says so, the login-code directory (threat 4). Since #708, named follow-ups
  rather than defects: doctor's job-folder check judges the tokens file's path and not the login-code directory
  beside it (a job folder that contains the file contains the directory too; one that IS the directory, or lies
  inside it, is not caught); the Windows opener (`rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler`) is verified by reading, not
  run; a pi attached through tmux from an SSH session can carry a local environment and open the browser on the
  host's unattended desktop; a minted link stays visible in the operator's notice and, until it is spent, in the
  browser's history (the console's script removes the fragment from history before it posts the code); `open` and
  `xdg-open` hand the redirect page to the desktop's `.html` handler, which may not be the browser, and on Linux a snap
  or Flatpak browser has a private `/tmp` and cannot read it (the notice says "handed to your browser", never
  "opened", and names that case with a pointer to the printed link); and one-time links are not supported on a
  Windows host, since Node reports group and other bits on every Windows file and directory and the drop is refused
  there (a token is pasted instead). Since #641: a token holder, a viewer included, who signs in eight times can
  hold all 32 stream slots, so other people's pages still load and still sign in but are not live until those
  streams close or that token's sessions end (`token revoke` or `rotate`); and a page that is only watched signs
  out at the idle limit, by design (an open stream never extends a session). Since #642: an operator's answer is
  quoted on the forge under the deployment's identity, so an operator token can put text on any parked issue the
  deployment can comment on (mentions neutralised, the author named); a bulk action can start up to 100 paid
  retries from one confirm, each still reserved and refused by the worker's caps; and a panel write made from a
  shell that cannot append to the audit log is refused, so a full or unwritable `PI_LOGS_DIR` stops the TUI's and
  the tools' writes until it is fixed. Since #643: the live transcript shows what the worker published, so a secret
  the agent transformed (`DES-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`'s residual) reaches an operator's page, and a transcript tab
  holds one of its token's stream slots like any live page.
