## DES-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM

- **Status**: issue #643 (2026-10-16), resolving `OQ-044`. The worker half (the live file, the tailer, the
  redactor, the stream) and the readers (the read model, the `/dispatch` panel) are built; the console's route and
  run page are `DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`'s, amended the same day.
- **Decision**: the worker tails each running job's pi session file and publishes a redacted, compact copy of it to
  one capped Valkey stream per job, so an operator can watch what a run is doing from the console on any host and
  from the `/dispatch` panel. Six parts:
  1. **A live file for every job, through the existing session contract.** A job that is not a resume job now gets
     `<jobDir>/session/current.jsonl`, staged empty (directory 0700, file 0600, `stageLiveFile` in
     `worker/src/live-transcript.mjs`), mounted at `/session` with `PI_SESSION_FILE=/session/current.jsonl`, the same
     layout `resolveSession` stages for a resume job. On an empty file the runner opens a fresh session at that path
     (`image/runner/src/session.mjs`), the path a cold-starting resume job already takes, so **the job image needs no
     change**. pi then appends one JSON line per entry as the agent works. A resume job is untouched: its staged
     transcript is its live file. The file has no store key, is never promoted, is removed by the sandbox retention
     before a run is kept, and is deleted with the job directory. Whether a job RESUMES stays keyed on
     `prepared.session` alone (the await-input arming, the promotion and the record's `session` read nothing
     else), so a non-resume job's run record is byte-identical to one written before the feature: the runner now
     reports `absent` for it (it found an empty file), and `mergeSession` maps exactly that report, for a job with a
     live file and no resolved session, back to `disabled`, the reason the runner gave for such a job before, because
     the object describes resuming and the job was never armed to resume. A staging that fails is logged
     (`live_transcript_unstaged`) and the job runs as every job did before, with no file and no stream.
  2. **The tailer** (`makeLiveTranscript`), started by `runContainer` when the container spawns. The file is the
     agent's (`/session` is mounted read-write), so the agent can replace it with a symlink to a host path or a FIFO,
     and the worker reads as its own account: following a link would publish whatever host file it named, another
     job's stored transcript being exactly pi-shaped. So each read `lstat`s first and refuses anything but a regular
     file, opens with `O_NOFOLLOW` and `O_NONBLOCK` (a link or FIFO swapped in after the `lstat` is refused, not
     followed or waited on), and refuses an open descriptor whose inode is not the one judged; a refusal is published
     once as a fixed note and the file is never read again for that job. It polls: an `lstat`
     every 500 ms and a read of the bytes appended since its offset, at most 4 MiB a poll. A line is complete at its
     newline; a partial last line is held until it completes. A size below the offset, a new inode, or a first line
     that changed means the file was rewritten (pi's header rewrite, a runner truncating an unparseable resume file):
     a `reset` entry is published and the file is read again from 0. A line over 1 MiB is never parsed; one
     `skipped` entry says so, and the rest of it is dropped as it arrives. A line that is not JSON becomes one fixed
     `note` ("a transcript line that is not JSON was left out"), never its bytes.
     **AMENDED 2026-10-19 (issue #686 part 1): a second source, pushed lines.** On a venue that copies the session
     file into its sandbox (`openshell`, `DES-OPENSHELL-VENUE`) there is no host file to tail while the job runs, so
     `makeLiveTranscript({ source: "stdio" })` is driven by lines `runContainer` pushes from the runner's signed stderr
     records (`worker/src/stderr-transcript.mjs`) instead: `setBaseline(size)`, `push(line, end)`, `skip(count)` for
     a gap in the records, and `reset(size)` for the runner's reset record. Each pushed line takes the tailed line's
     own path (`publishLine`: the parse, `onParsed`, the mapping, the redactor, the bounds), with the runner's own
     `end` (the file offset past its newline), so positions stay exact across a gap; the timer only flushes, and
     `finish` flushes and publishes `end`. **The baseline is the runner's** (review of #709, same day): the session
     file's size when its mirror started, before pi loaded, sent as the first signed record. On `openshell` the
     session directory is uploaded, so a session-store resume puts the earlier conversation into the file, and its
     lines end at or before that size: `prior`, as the file tail's `lstat` at spawn makes them, so progress and the
     status comment do not count the earlier turns. `onBaseline` fires once the lines up to it are in (at once for an
     empty file), failing open at the first line when the baseline record was broken (nothing is then `prior`), at a
     reset or at `finish`. Taken from the runner rather than from the host's staged copy read before the upload
     (REJECTED): the runner's is the file the lines are read from, after anything the runner did to it before pi
     loaded, and it rides the same signed channel, in order, before any line. After a reset, the lines ending at or
     before the reset's size (the runner's) are `replay`, the rule a rewritten file gets. No checkpoint is opened on
     it (the checkpointer copies a host file). The file tail is UNCHANGED, checked, for every binding venue.
  3. **The mapping**, one pi entry to the display entries it becomes (`entriesOf`), against the pinned pi's
     session-manager shapes: a user message is `user`; an assistant message is one `assistant` entry for its text
     (when not blank) plus one `tool-call` per tool call, whose text is the arguments JSON-stringified; a tool result
     (and pi's own `bashExecution`) is `tool-result`, its text parts joined by newlines and each image as `[image]`,
     flagged when pi marked it an error; a compaction or branch summary is `compaction`; a model change, a thinking
     level change, a context edit and a custom message are one short `note` each. **Never published**: the model's
     thinking (a model's private reasoning is not shown); the session header's `cwd` (the header becomes the note
     "session started"); `usage`, `custom`, `session_info` and `label` entries; a provider's error message (an
     assistant turn that ended in `error` or `aborted` becomes a note naming only that stop reason token).
  4. **The redactor** (`makeRedactor` and `secretValuesOf`, `worker/src/redact-secrets.mjs`), built per job in
     `runContainer` from the job's own container env, and applied to every text before it is escaped and cut.
     - **The key rule is inverted**: every container env key is secret-bearing unless it is in
       `NON_SECRET_ENV_KEYS`, the structural keys `buildContainerEnv` writes (paths, flags, model names, counts, the
       forge host variables, derived from their sources), held to the builder by a test. The proxy variables are
       structural only when their value is exactly what the worker's `egressEnv` wrote for this job: an operator who
       forwards `HTTPS_PROXY` with credentials (`PI_EGRESS=0`) gets them redacted (`secretValuesOf`'s `workerSet`). So the minted
       forge token under each name, the provider credential, every `PI_FORWARD_ENV` value, every resolved trigger
       secret and every model-endpoint key are redacted by construction, and a key added to the env later is
       redacted until someone lists it: a missing entry costs readability, never a leak. The minted `token` and the
       `exitKey` (which never enters the env) are added explicitly.
     - **Rule 1, values**: each secret value of at least 8 characters in its literal, JSON-escaped (as
       `JSON.stringify` writes it inside a string, which is how tool arguments reach the stream) and URL-encoded
       (`encodeURIComponent`, both hex cases) forms, longest first, so a value containing another is taken whole.
       Shorter values are a port, a flag or a word, and replacing them would shred the text.
     - **Rule 2, shapes**, for a secret this job was never handed: GitHub's `ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `ghr_` and
       `github_pat_`, GitLab's `glpat-`, `sk-ant-` and `sk-` keys, Slack's `xoxb-` and `xoxp-`, this project's console
       tokens (`pdc_`), AWS access key ids (`AKIA...`), and the credential half of an `Authorization:` header or a bare
       `Bearer`, keeping the scheme. Each body has a length floor and a left anchor, so `sk-learn` or `task-...` stays.
     - **Rule 3, URL userinfo**: `scheme://user:password@` becomes `scheme://[redacted]@`; the scheme is required, so an
       e-mail address is left alone. And the password inside a URL-shaped secret value (a forwarded proxy) is a value
       of its own, raw and percent-decoded, so a tool printing it without its URL (`curl -U user:password`) is caught.
       The `Authorization` header rule also takes a quoted credential after its scheme and a header with no scheme.
     - A match becomes `[redacted]`. Redaction runs on an entry's WHOLE text when the entry is queued, before any cut,
       so no cut can split a secret; a redactor that throws drops that entry rather than publish its raw text.
  5. **Escaping and caps.** After redaction every text has its control and bidi characters written out as
     `\u{XXXX}` (the worker's `escapeControls`), except that real newlines and tabs stay real characters, so a
     multi-line message or tool output stays multi-line for a reader (`\r\n` and a lone `\r` become `\n`). Then it
     is cut to 4,096 code points (8,192 for an `assistant` text), never inside an escape, and flagged `truncated`.
     The tool name is redacted too and keeps its charset (`[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}`), else it becomes `?`; a name
     redaction changed is published as `?` (the model chooses tool names, and a token fits the charset). `ts` is the pi
     entry's own timestamp when it lies between 0 and a day ahead, else the publish time.
  6. **The stream** (`INT-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`): `run:live:<sanitized job id>`, through the sanitizer the run
     mirror uses for `runs:rec:`. Each poll writes what it read in one `MULTI`: `XADD ... MAXLEN ~ 2000 *` per entry,
     and at an attempt's first write a `DEL` of the key first (a retry reuses the job id, so the previous attempt's
     stream is deleted and a stream holds one attempt) and a `PEXPIRE` of 7 days, so a worker that dies mid-run
     cannot leave it forever. The key exists about one poll after the container starts. Every Valkey call is bounded
     (1 s) and best effort: a failure drops and counts the batch, at most 2,000 entries and 8 MiB of field values wait for a
     write (the oldest dropped past either), and nothing here throws into, fails or slows the job. **The end**: when the container
     exits, `runContainer` calls `finish(outcome)` in its `close` handler, BEFORE its promise resolves and so before
     the processor's `finally` removes the job directory: it waits for a poll in flight, reads the file to its end
     (a partial last line taken as a line), flushing after every chunk, at most 64 MiB (`LIVE_FINAL_READ_MAX_BYTES`,
     then `skipped` once), so a huge or sparse file the agent made cannot keep the worker reading or hold its memory, publishes `end` with the outcome and sets a `PEXPIRE` of 24 h,
     all bounded at 3 s whatever Valkey does. Once `finish` settles, done or timed out, the publisher is closed: no read
     starts, nothing is queued and nothing is written, so a stale attempt can never write into a retry's stream (a
     timed-out finish loses its `end`; residual: a transaction already handed to the client before it settled can
     still be resent by ioredis after a reconnect). The outcome is the exit's own reading (`liveOutcomeOf`): exit 0
     `completed`, exit 1 `failed`, exit 2 or a worker abort `policy`, anything else `unknown`; a container that never
     started ends `failed`. It is what `runContainer` knows, and it can differ from the run record's
     classification, which the processor makes afterwards with more (an exit 1 classified as an infra retry, an OOM
     confirmed by the supervisor, a completed run the cost settlement refuses); the record stays the authority.
- **Logging**: the publisher logs the job id and counts only (`live_transcript_write_failed` once per job,
  `live_transcript_ended` with `published`, `dropped`, `skipped`, `notes`, `resets`, `errors`, `refused`), never an entry's
  content (`no-pii-in-logs`).
- **The off switch**: `PI_LIVE_TRANSCRIPTS`. Unset, empty or `1` publishes; `0` publishes nothing (the opener is null,
  and no live file is staged either, so a job without a resume transcript runs exactly as before the feature, its
  session in memory and no `/session` mount). Any other value refuses to boot, for
  `globalExtensionsEnabled`'s reason: `PI_LIVE_TRANSCRIPTS=false` read as on would be an operator believing PII
  stays on the host while it does not. Documented in both `.env.example` files, which the env-docs test holds.
  **Since issue #644 the switch governs the stream only** (`DES-RUN-PROGRESS`): the same file is read for run
  progress unless `PI_RUN_PROGRESS=0`, so the opener is null, and the live file left unstaged, only when BOTH are `0`.
  With `PI_LIVE_TRANSCRIPTS=0` and progress on, the tailer runs exactly as above (the same refusals, polls, resets and
  final read) with its stream mode off (`stream: false`): every parsed line goes to the progress reducer and nothing is
  queued or written, so no `run:live:` key is touched, no `end` is written and no transcript text reaches Valkey. The
  progress key then carries only counts, checked tool names and, for a job armed with `run.progress`, its redacted
  phase names and note.
- **The progress hook** (issue #644): `makeLiveTranscript` takes `onParsed(parsed, ts, { prior, replay })` and
  `onReset()`. Each complete line's parsed object is handed to `onParsed` before and apart from the mapping above (so
  the reducer reads the fields `entriesOf` drops: `toolCallId`, `durationMs`, the call arguments), never once the
  publisher is closed, and a throw from it is swallowed. `prior` marks a line that ended at or before the BASELINE, the
  file's size when the first read began (one `lstat`; anything but a regular file is 0), which on a resume is the
  earlier runs' transcript; after a reset there is no prior any more, and `replay` marks a line that ended at or
  before the rewritten file's size at the reset. The `ts` handed to `onParsed` is the line's timestamp bounded as the
  stream's `ts` is (from 0 to a day past the read time, else the read time), since the reducer keeps it as a step's
  `since`. The baseline `lstat` runs only when a hook is given, so without one the file is read exactly as before.
- **The checkpoint consumer** (issue #645, `DES-RUN-CHECKPOINT-PAIRED`): `onParsed`'s flags gain `end`, the file
  position just past the line's newline (absent for the final read's unterminated tail, which ends at no newline), so
  a consumer knows a complete-line boundary. The opener takes `checkpoint`, the run checkpointer's `open`; for an
  attempt `runContainer` hands open arguments (a `run.recover` job the processor armed), its handle is the THIRD
  consumer of every parsed line, beside the progress sink, each guarded on its own so a throw in one never starves the
  other, and is reset with the file. It turns the tailing on by itself: start.mjs builds the opener whenever a run
  checkpointer exists, and an armed job with both switches off still has its file staged and tailed with
  `stream: false` and no progress sink, because its live checkpoints are driven by its lines. The handle is not closed
  by the opener's finish but by `runContainer`, before the final read, so no live checkpoint pauses a dead container.
  **Since #645 the stream's key is the RUN id** (`runIdOf`: `recoveryOf` for a recovery job `<runId>.r<n>`, else the
  job id), so a recovery continues its run's stream: its first write replaces the lost attempt's entries, as a
  retry's does.
- **Why**: the console (#640 to #642) shows every run's record fleet-wide and nothing of what a run is doing. The raw
  log exists only with `PI_CAPTURE_JOB_LOGS=1` and only on the host that ran the job, runner stdout carries id-only
  events, and before this only `run.resume` jobs wrote a transcript file at all. The transcript is the artifact that
  answers "what is it doing", it is structured (no terminal escapes to parse), and pi already writes it, so the
  worker only has to read a file it mounted. The worker, not the runner, publishes because a container that could
  write to Valkey would be a new network path out of the box (`CONST-ISOLATION-CONTAINER-PER-JOB`); reading from
  this side adds no route, and the file is in the job's own directory. A poll, not `fs.watch`, because the file is a
  bind mount that crosses a VM on Docker Desktop and Podman machine, where change events are dropped or late. The
  transcript is agent-writable, like stdout (#542, #545), so it is untrusted data at every step: redacted before it
  leaves, escaped by every surface, interpreted by none.
- **Rejected**:
  - **The runner publishing** over a new network path from the container. It is a route out of the box for the
    agent's process tree, with a credential to Valkey inside it, against `CONST-ISOLATION-CONTAINER-PER-JOB`; the
    worker already has the file.
  - **Mirroring the raw log.** It carries terminal escapes, the runner's own lines and whatever a tool printed, with
    no structure to redact or cap by, and it is the artifact `docs/multi-host.md` keeps on its host on purpose.
  - **Local only** (the other answer to `OQ-044`): a console on one host of a fleet, or on a machine that is not a
    worker, would answer "not on this host" for most runs.
  - **A blocking `XREAD` on the reader's shared client.** The fleet reader holds one client for the whole snapshot,
    and a `BLOCK` read would park every read of the next tick behind it; a second connection per open tail is a
    cost and a cap to manage. Readers use non-blocking `XRANGE` at their own refresh rhythm.
  - **Shipping the thinking.** A model's private reasoning is not what an operator watches for, it is the part
    most likely to restate a secret it saw, and it is not shown on any other surface.
  - **Auditing transcript reads.** The console's audit vocabulary is writes and refusals; a read row per open tail
    would be a new kind of row for a read the role guard already bounds. Considered, not built.
- **Residuals**, stated rather than implied (each is in `SECURITY.md`):
  - **A transformed secret is not caught**: base64, reversed, split across two tool calls, one character per line.
    No rule that does not know the transformation can catch it. Redaction bounds an accident; it is not a boundary
    against an agent trying to leak.
  - **The tail can be lost when the abort grace runs out**: a cancelled or timed-out job whose container does not
    close within the abort grace lets the processor clean up before `finish` runs, so the run's last lines and its
    `end` entry are not published; the stream then expires on its 7-day TTL.
  - **A rewrite to the same first line at a larger size** is not seen as a reset; pi rewrites only on a format
    migration or a branch, neither of which a job does after its header.
  - Readers see a stream at most one poll (about 500 ms) behind the file, and a Valkey outage loses the entries
    written during it.
- **Traces to**: `REQ-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT`, `REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY`, `INT-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`, `INT-SESSION-STORE-CONTRACT`,
  `INT-CONTAINER-JOB-INPUTS`, `INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT`, `DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`, `DES-ADMIN-VIA-PI-EXTENSION`,
  `CONST-ISOLATION-CONTAINER-PER-JOB`, `CONST-ISSUE-TEXT-IS-DATA`, `OQ-044`.

  admin/src/dashboard.ts (LIVE_TAIL), admin/src/index.ts (`panelTailLog`). Since #644: worker/src/live-transcript.mjs
  (`onParsed`, `onReset`, `stream`, and the opener's `transcripts`, `progress` and `makeCommenter`). Since #686:
  worker/src/live-transcript.mjs (`source: "stdio"`, `push`, `skip`, `reset`), worker/src/stderr-transcript.mjs.

## DES-RUN-PROGRESS

- **Status**: issue #644 (2026-10-16). The worker half (the reducer, the key, the record field, the switch), the job
  tool (runner, image, triggers, receiver, preflight, the admin's trigger tools) and the forge status comment (the
  hosts, the commenter, the wiring) are built, and so are the readers, the console's displays and the panel's ACTIVE
  rows, recorded in `DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE` and `DES-ADMIN-VIA-PI-EXTENSION`.
- **Decision**: the worker reads where each running job is from the pi session file it already tails for the live
  transcript (`DES-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`), keeps a small summary in one Valkey key per job, copies its integers into
  the run record, and, for a forge trigger that opts in, renders it into one forge comment it edits. Five parts:
  1. **Automatic steps, for every job** (`makeProgress`, `worker/src/run-progress.mjs`, fed every parsed line by the
     tailer's `onParsed`). pi 1.2.0 saves each message at `message_end`: an assistant message is one TURN and carries
     its tool calls (`{type: "toolCall", id, name, arguments}`); each result is a `toolResult` message with
     `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `isError` and, when the tool actually ran, `durationMs` (pi-agent-core
     `createToolResultMessage`). So a turn opens one STEP per call, keyed by its id, with the tool and the entry's time,
     and the result closes it as `ok` or `error` with its own `durationMs`, null when pi wrote none (an unknown tool, a
     validation failure). A call with no result yet is RUNNING. A result whose id is unknown, already closed, or a call
     id reused, is ignored and counted as an anomaly (logged in the counts only), and so is a call or result whose id
     is longer than 128 UTF-16 units (`PROGRESS_ID_MAX`): an id is a map key held while its step is open, so a forged
     line holding one id of nearly a megabyte would otherwise pin that megabyte, 256 times over. An assistant message
     whose `stopReason` is `"error"` or `"aborted"` opens no step (pi returns before it runs any tool, and the half
     streamed calls stay in the saved message, so they would read as running and then as interrupted); an `"error"`
     message is not a turn either and an `"aborted"` one is, which is how the runner counts turns (`turn-budget.mjs`:
     a provider error and its retry count once). The time a step opens at is the line's own timestamp bounded as the
     stream's `ts` is (from 0 to a day past the read, else the read time), since the line is the agent's to write.
     When the container ends, every call still open becomes `interrupted`. Memory is bounded: 256 open calls (the
     oldest dropped and counted), a ring of 20 recent steps, 8 running listed, 32 phase names, each key at most 128
     units. The display name of a tool is the stream's charset
     (`LIVE_TOOL_RE`) else `?`, and `?` when the job's redactor would change it; the record's name is a bucket of a
     closed list, compared and never copied.
  2. **Resume and rewrite awareness.** On a resume the file starts with the earlier runs' entries. The tailer takes
     the file's size before its first read as the BASELINE; lines ending at or before it seed `prior: {turns, steps}`
     and the phase list and current phase, never this attempt's counters, so a resumed run continues its phases and
     still counts its own turns from 1. A retry (same job id, a fresh job directory) starts over, as the stream does. A
     RESET (the file rewritten, read again from 0) keeps the counts already seen: the rewritten file's bytes up to its
     size at the reset are REPLAYED and count nothing, except a result that closes a call still open, since that call
     is this attempt's and its result arrived inside the rewrite. A call and result both written and rewritten between
     two polls can be lost; pi rewrites only on a format migration or a branch, neither of which a job does.
  3. **Phases, opt-in per trigger** (`run.progress`). The job is offered `report_progress`
     (`image/runner/src/report-progress.mjs`), an inline extension factory registered only when `PI_REPORT_PROGRESS=1`,
     with a shadow guard and a `tool_call` hook like `await_human_input`'s and no `terminate`: it validates
     `{phase (1 to 64 code points, not blank), done? (integer from 0), total? (integer from 1), note? (at most 200 code
     points)}`, `done <= total`, no other key, and answers "recorded", or an error result naming the fault. It has no
     side effect: what it reports lives only in the transcript. The reducer reads a call's arguments only for a job
     with `job.progress` and applies them only when the call's result arrives with `isError: false`, so a report the
     runner refused is ignored. It re-validates the same bounds (with `done` and `total` at most 1,000,000, which the
     runner does not cap), and ignores a call that fails them whole. The phase list keeps names in first-seen order
     (a new name past 32 leaves the current phase as it was); the current phase is the index, `done` and `total`; the
     note is the latest. Phase names and notes are model text: redacted with the job's redactor, control and bidi
     characters written out (`escapeControls`), cut to 64 and 200 code points; a redactor that throws drops the report.
  4. **The key** (`makeProgressWriter`, `INT-RUN-PROGRESS-KEY`): `run:progress:<id>`, the whole snapshot as one JSON
     string, written on change at most once a second with a trailing write, best effort and bounded like the stream's
     writes (1 s a call), 7 days from the attempt's first write and 24 hours after the final one, capped at 16 KiB.
     `updatedAt` is the time of the write that carried it, and until the final write the snapshot is written again
     every 30 s (`PROGRESS_HEARTBEAT_MS`) even when nothing moved, so a reader can tell a quiet run (a long tool, a slow
     model) from a worker that died without its final write: readers call a key stale when it has not ended and its
     `updatedAt` is older than 180 s (`PROGRESS_STALE_MS`, admin/src/read-model.mjs). The first write of an attempt
     waits for one bounded read of the key an earlier attempt left and keeps its `commentId`; it is made at the sink's
     start with the empty snapshot (turn 0), so a retry replaces the final snapshot of the attempt before it at once
     rather than at its first transcript line. The FINISH (`makeProgressSink.finish`) runs inside the opener's finish,
     after the stream's own (bounded at 3 s), so no line reaches the reducer after it: it hands the final snapshot
     (open calls `interrupted`, `ended`, the exit's outcome) to the commenter, waits at most 2 s for a comment post
     still in flight so its id rides the final write (the key is closed after it, and a retry that read no id would
     post a second comment), then writes it with the 24 h TTL, all bounded together at 5 s. Worst case at a run's end:
     3 s plus 5 s, the 5 s only when Valkey or the forge hangs.
  5. **The record and the comment.** `runContainer` returns the reducer's `summary()` as `progress`, and the
     processor carries it to `buildRecord` on every result and on a thrown error (as it does `resources`), and a
     spent attempt that ends as an operator cancel instead of a retry keeps it (`endCancelled`, index.mjs), where
     `recordedProgress` rebuilds it into integers and closed keys (`INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT`). `toolMs` is the
     SUM of the closed steps' durations (steps of a parallel batch overlap, so it can pass the run's wall time), and
     `longestInterruptedMs` the longest a step still open at the end had run. For a forge job
     whose trigger set `run.statusComment`, the opener asks start.mjs for a commenter
     (`makeStatusCommenter`, `worker/src/status-comment.mjs`, `INT-FORGE-STATUS-COMMENT-EDIT`), created at the sink's
     start after the key's read so a retry edits the first attempt's comment, and fed each snapshot the writer writes;
     it throttles its own edits to one per 30 s. Its FINAL edit comes from the run record, not from the exit: the exit
     code is a weaker reading than the record's classification (an OOM kill exits 137 and is recorded `policy`; an
     infrastructure exit is retried under the same job id). start.mjs registers each commenter in a registry
     (`makeStatusCommentRegistry`) by job id; the sink's finish hands it the final snapshot, and `recordRun` settles it
     with the record's outcome, or with "attempt ended, retrying" (`STATUS_RETRYING`) for an `InfraRetry` with
     attempts left. An attempt that leaves no record (a hold, a record path that threw) is finished 5 minutes after
     the container ended (`STATUS_FALLBACK_MS`; it was 30 s, which a slow record path could lose to, locking in the
     exit's weaker reading) with the exit's outcome, so the comment never says "running" after the run; a record that
     settles after that fallback, within 10 minutes (`STATUS_LATE_SETTLE_MS`, at most 256 such commenters kept), makes
     one corrective edit when its text differs. A new attempt's commenter replaces the entry without a final edit and
     edits the same comment. An attempt that registers no commenter at all (one refused before its container, after
     an earlier attempt posted the comment and left it saying "attempt ended, retrying") is edited by `recordRun`
     itself: one bounded `GET` of the key for the earlier attempt's `commentId`, then one bounded edit with the
     record's outcome and the key's last snapshot (`settleUnregisteredStatus`), skipped on a phrase collision and when
     the key holds no id.
- **Recovered runs** (issue #645, `DES-RECOVERY-REPLAY-CLASSES`). A recovering runner answers the calls the loss cut
  off with results marked `details.piDispatchRecovery` (`interrupted`, `not-started` or `replayed`). Those calls were
  made by the lost attempt, so they open no step here. A marked result closes a step still open under its id without
  counting a step; `interrupted` and `not-started` count as `interrupted` (the word this reducer already uses for a
  call whose result never came) and are listed in `recent`; `replayed` is its own count, written to the key and the
  record only above zero, so every other key and record keeps its field set; an unknown mark is an ordinary result;
  on a replay pass a marked result for a call not open counts nothing. The mark is read from an agent-writable file
  like everything here: advisory. The progress key, like the stream, is spelled from the RUN id, so a recovery reads
  its run's `commentId` and edits the same status comment, and the lost attempt's record settles that comment as
  retrying (`recovery-enqueued`).
- **The recovery marks split by word** (issue #662). Because `interrupted` merges two marks with the steps still open
  at the end, the reducer also counts `recoveryInterrupted` and `recoveryNotStarted`: the `interrupted` and
  `not-started` marks alone, on this attempt's lines only (a prior line's mark goes to the prior, and a replay pass
  counts nothing, as for `replayed`). They are extra `summary()` keys, a zero left out, and NEVER in the snapshot (the
  admin's strict parser would refuse the key whole) nor in the record's `progress` (`recordedProgress` keeps
  `PROGRESS_COUNT_KEYS`, which does not list them). Their one reader is the processor: a recovery whose container
  wrote no exit line (it was killed) takes its record's `recovered` counts from them, `orphans` the sum of the three,
  labelled `countsFrom: "transcript"`; the runner's exit line's counts win whenever it carries a `recovery` block. Rejected: adding them to
  `progress` (a second copy of the same counts, which a reader could add up twice), and taking a zero from the
  transcript (it cannot tell "nothing orphaned" from "killed before the runner answered anything", so the counts stay
  null). The same issue reads the key from the stall listener: the crashed attempt's record takes its `startedAt` and
  integer counts from the run's key, read before the recovery replaces it, when the key has not ended and its start is
  not after now and no earlier than the stalled job's enqueue time, which ties the key to that job: a recovery that died
  before its own first write must not take the base attempt's key (`INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT`); `processedOn` was the rejected source, since BullMQ's stall re-pick
  overwrites it.
- **Advisory, never trusted.** `/session` is mounted read-write, so the agent can write any line into the file this
  reads, and a forged line costs nothing (#545 is the same class for stdout). Progress therefore decides nothing: no
  classification, budget, exit outcome, retry, alert or gate reads it, every field is bounded so a forged file cannot
  grow it, and a forged `report_progress` call can at most show a false phase to an operator. The record's copy is
  integers under closed keys, and the comment's text is fixed words and integers, so a forgery cannot put a string
  into either.
- **The off switch**: `PI_RUN_PROGRESS`. Unset, empty or `1` reads progress; `0` turns off the key, the record field
  and the comment; anything else refuses to boot, for `PI_LIVE_TRANSCRIPTS`' reason. Independent of
  `PI_LIVE_TRANSCRIPTS` (the file is staged when either is on). It does not change what a job is offered: a job armed
  with `run.progress` still gets the tool and is still held to the image capability with progress off, and a trigger's
  `run.statusComment` then posts nothing. Documented in both `.env.example` files, which the env-docs test holds.
- **Logging**: job ids, reasons and counts only, never a phase name, note, tool name or comment text
  (`run_progress_write_failed`, the `status_comment_*` events of `INT-FORGE-STATUS-COMMENT-EDIT`, among them
  `status_comment_skipped` with `progress-off`, `no-transcript`, `no-forge-target` or `phrase-collision`).
- **Why**: the live transcript (#643) shows everything a run does and summarises nothing; an operator watching a fleet
  needs "turn 40, a test command running ten minutes, phase 3 of 5" at a glance, and the requester on the issue sees
  nothing between the start and the end. Everything the automatic part needs is already in a file the worker reads,
  so it costs no image change and no new path; a phase is the one fact only the agent has, so it is a tool call that
  lands in the same file. Reading it on the worker side keeps the container without a network path, for the reason the
  stream is published from there.
- **Rejected**:
  - **Runner stdout as the transport.** It is forgeable by any tool child exactly as the exit line was before #545,
    carries no structure, and would need a second parser beside the transcript the worker already reads.
  - **A runner network path** (the container writing progress to Valkey or the worker over a socket): a route out of
    the box for the agent's process tree, against `CONST-ISOLATION-CONTAINER-PER-JOB`, to carry what the file already
    holds.
  - **Phase text in the record or the comment.** The record's PII-free property rests on holding no attacker-chosen
    string, and a phase name is model text; a public comment must not carry text that could mention a user or hold a
    link. Both carry the phase's INDEX and the list's LENGTH instead.
  - **Per-tool live status inside a parallel batch.** pi saves a batch's results together once the whole batch is
    done (pi-agent-core `agent-loop.js`), so the file shows every call of a batch running until all finish; durations
    come from `durationMs`, never from the results' shared timestamp. Not observable from the file, so not shown.
  - **Timestamps as durations**, for the same reason, and because a result that failed before it ran has no
    duration at all: null is shown, not a guess.
  - **Trusting the agent's `done`/`total` for anything.** They are drawn as a bar and counted nowhere.
- **Residuals**, stated rather than implied (each is in `SECURITY.md`):
  - A false phase or count: the agent can write any line into its transcript, so an operator can be shown a phase or a
    step count that did not happen. Bounded to display.
  - A phase name or note can carry text the agent read (issue text, a file); it is redacted like the transcript and
    shares its residual (a transformed secret is not caught), and it is shown to the operator role alone.
  - The status comment is a public edit stream on the issue: it reveals how long a run took, how many turns and steps
    and whether steps failed, to everyone who can read the issue. That is why it is opt-in and off by default.
  - #645's synthetic interrupted results are counted as ordinary results until their shape is settled
    (marked in `run-progress.mjs`'s `finalSnapshot`).
  - A job whose container outlives the abort grace (a stop that did not take) gets no exit to read. When the
    processor gives up on it (`boundAfterAbort`, `stop_did_not_take`), it finishes the attempt's live publisher itself
    through the finish runContainer handed it (`onLive`), with outcome `unknown`, and waits for that (bounded, 10 s)
    before it records and removes the job directory, so the key gets its final write with `ended` and the heartbeat
    stops; it once kept rewriting the key as running for as long as the worker lived. A worker that dies (a crash, a
    kill) writes nothing more, heartbeat included, so its key lives out its 7 days without `ended` and readers call it
    stale 180 s after its last write. As a bound behind both, the writer stops every write but the final one 7 days
    after it started (`run_progress_expired`), so no heartbeat outlives the key's window and no write sets a TTL under
    a second.
  - An operator's cancel of a delayed retry removes the job from the CLI (`pi-dispatch cancel`) and writes no record,
    so no worker edits the status comment again and it keeps saying "attempt ended, retrying".
- **Traces to**: `REQ-RUN-PROGRESS`, `REQ-JOB-STATUS-COMMENTS`, `INT-RUN-PROGRESS-KEY`,
  `INT-FORGE-STATUS-COMMENT-EDIT`, `INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT`, `INT-TRIGGERS-FILE-CONTRACT`,
  `INT-RUNNER-EXIT-CODE-PROTOCOL`, `INT-CONTAINER-RUNTIME-CONTRACT`, `DES-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`,
  `DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`, `DES-ADMIN-VIA-PI-EXTENSION`, `DES-AWAIT-INPUT-ENDS-THE-JOB`,
  `CONST-ISOLATION-CONTAINER-PER-JOB`, `CONST-ISSUE-TEXT-IS-DATA`, `CONST-BUDGET-BEFORE-TOKENS`.
- **Code evidence**: worker/src/run-progress.mjs (`makeProgress`, `serializeProgress`, `makeProgressWriter`,
  `makeProgressSink`, `recordToolOf`, the `PROGRESS_*` constants, exported as `@edgehero/pi-dispatch/run-progress`),
  worker/src/live-transcript.mjs (`onParsed`, the baseline, `replay`, `stream: false`, the opener),
  worker/src/status-comment.mjs (`renderStatusText`, `makeStatusCommenter`, `makeStatusCommentRegistry`,
  `STATUS_RETRYING`, `STATUS_FALLBACK_MS`, `commentIdOf`),
  worker/src/{github,gitlab,forgejo,azure}-host.mjs (`postStatusComment`'s `{ id }`, `editStatusComment`),
  worker/src/start.mjs (`statusPost`, `statusEdit`, `makeProgressCommenter`, `statusTextMayMatch`, the registry and
  `recordRun`'s settle, `settleUnregisteredStatus`, the opener's two switches, `stageLive`), worker/src/index.mjs
  (`endCancelled` keeps `progress`, `boundAfterAbort`'s awaited give-up hook finishing the publisher),
  worker/src/run-container.mjs (`reportProgress`, `progress` off `progressSummary`, `onLive`),
  worker/src/processor.mjs (`progress` on every result, the `report-progress-shadowed` comment),
  worker/src/run-history.mjs (`recordedProgress`, `PROGRESS_RECORD_TOOLS`, `PROGRESS_RUNNER_REASONS`),
  worker/src/config.mjs (`runProgressEnabled`), worker/src/triggers.mjs (`validateProgressFlags`),
  worker/src/triggers-file.mjs, worker/src/queue.mjs, worker/src/schedules.mjs, worker/src/env-allowlist.mjs,
  worker/src/reserved-env.mjs, worker/src/redact-secrets.mjs, worker/src/image-preflight.mjs (the `reportProgress`
  row), image/runner/src/report-progress.mjs, image/runner/src/config.mjs, image/runner/run-job.mjs, image/Dockerfile,
  image/verify-image.sh, receiver/src/config.mjs and the four filters, admin/src/write-plans.mjs, admin/src/index.ts
  (the trigger tools' parameters), admin/src/job-actions.mjs (`runFieldsOf`). admin/src/read-model.mjs,
  admin/src/console/ (panels.mjs, pages.mjs, live.mjs), admin/src/dashboard.ts.

## DES-TERMINAL-CHAT

- **Status**: issue #647, part 1 (2026-10-18): the terminal client `pi-dispatch chat`, the console's `GET /api/run`,
  the JSON transcript format and the run page's Chat panel; part 2 (2026-10-18): `/dispatch chat` in the pi
  extension (part 6 below).
- **Decision**: a run's chat opens in a terminal through **the console, as a browser client would**, for the live and
  reply modes, and **on the session store's own host, read directly**, for the fork. Six parts:
  1. **One mode rule.** `chatModeOf` (`worker/src/chat-mode.mjs`) is pure and total and takes the facts the caller read
     (the job's BullMQ state, its record, its active job, and for a parked record whether a later run took the
     answer). The CLI never judges a mode itself: it asks `/api/run`, whose `mode` comes from that function, and the
     run page's Chat panel calls the same function through `chatFactsOf`. Active wins over a record (an infra retry
     keeps the job id, so attempt 1's record can exist while attempt 2 runs) and a queued state wins too (a retry
     waiting to start is about to be the writer, and so is a #645 recovery job waiting to start: `liveJobsOfRun`
     reports it as `queuedAs`, since its base attempt's record says `recovery-enqueued`, which alone reads as finished
     and would offer a fork racing the recovery). A refusal is `{mode: null, says}` with a fixed sentence, never a
     bare null.
     - **"The same target" is ONE comparison**, `targetKeyOf` (`admin/src/read-model.mjs`): a forge target's
       repository path compared case-insensitively and its number without leading zeros, a local or cron target
       exactly (a folder name is case-sensitive). The parked fold's answered rule (`readParkedRuns`), the parked
       answer's planner, `/api/run`'s URL lookup and newer-run search, and the pending-answer scan all use it, so none
       can call a run answered that another offers a reply for.
     - **A park being answered.** The answered rule looks for a later RECORD, and a record is written at a run's end,
       so the answer's own resume run, queued or running, would leave the park offering a second reply that resumes
       the same transcript twice. A pending answer is found by a bounded queue scan (`readPendingOnTargets`: the
       active and queued jobs, each job's target compared by `targetKeyOf`, the park's own run excluded), not by the
       answer's keys: its delivery id is new for each answer, and its semantic window names the comment trigger's flow
       and lapses after ten minutes while the run may go on for an hour. A capped or failed list is unknown, and an
       unknown park is refused, never a reply. The planner, `/api/run` (`pendingRunOnTarget`), the Chat panel and the
       fleet reader's parked rows (`answering`, rescanned at most every 15 s while something is parked) share it.
       Review round 2: the scan pages every state, in the order a job moves through them, under ONE budget of 10,000
       listed ids (`PENDING_SCAN_BUDGET`; a cap of 200 per state had made any busy queue leave every park
       unanswerable, and a state holding exactly the cap read as partial), reads per id only the job hash's `name`
       (a `local` cron or CLI job is skipped at once) and `deid`, the semantic dedup id whose `repo<sep>number` prefix
       is `targetFor`'s target, parses `.data` only for a forge job without one (a recovery, a late message's job; at
       most `PENDING_DATA_MAX`), and stops once every target is matched; 1,200 paused jobs read in tens of
       milliseconds. **A queue past the budget fails loudly**, with its own sentence
       (`CHAT_REFUSALS.parkedTooMany`: answer on the forge, or wait), not the unread history's "try again".
       Rejected: failing open on it with the ten-minute semantic window as the backstop. The scan gives up only on a
       queue that deep, and there a queued answer can wait past those ten minutes, so the backstop has lapsed exactly
       when it would be needed. One mapping (`pendingFactsOf`, `parkedVerdictOf`, chat-mode.mjs) turns a scan into
       the verdict, so `/parked` draws a form for exactly the parks the Chat panel does.
     - **The reply form is the planner's.** The Chat panel offers it only where `planParkedAnswer` would plan the
       answer: the planner's own predicate over the retained job's data and the triggers file
       (`parkedAnswerRefusalOf`, through the fleet reader's `parkedAnswerCheck`, which hands back a sentence or ok,
       never the job's data), and the refusal sentence in its place otherwise.
     - **The newer-run search is a runs-page read**, so the run page's live loop reuses a parked record's answer for
       30 s per run id (`NEWER_CACHE_MS`; an unknown answer is not kept); `/api/run` never does. Review round 2: the
       loop reuses the pending scan and the planner check (`parkedAnswerCheckOf`) for 15 s per run id
       (`PARK_CHECK_CACHE_MS`, the snapshot's own rescan window; an unreadable one is not kept, a new record reads
       afresh), and when a scan finds the answer it saw before gone, the cached newer-run answer is dropped and
       searched again, so a finished answer's record is seen at once rather than after up to 30 s of a reply offered
       to an answered park. The planner still reads both afresh before anything is queued.
  2. **The console's auth model, unchanged.** The client (`worker/src/console-client.mjs`) signs in with `POST /login`
     and holds the `pdc_session` cookie in memory for the life of the process; it is never written anywhere. Every
     request carries `Host` (the address dialled; `localhost` over a unix socket, the one loopback name a socket has)
     and `Origin: http://<Host>`, and a write carries `Content-Type: application/json`. `Sec-Fetch-Site` is never sent:
     the console's origin guard accepts its absence as a non-browser client and judges `Origin` alone, and a client
     that claimed `same-origin` would be claiming to be the console's own page. Writes are the console's existing
     actions (`steer`, `steer-withdraw`, `parked-answer`), previewed, confirmed on screen (y/n) with the preview's
     ticket, and audited as the token's name, exactly as from the page.
  3. **The stream.** `GET /api/transcript?format=json` is the run page's operator-only stream with a structured entry
     (`transcriptEntryJson`, rebuilt by name) in place of the server-rendered HTML; the hub renders each entry once per
     format per tick, so an HTML and a JSON stream on one job cost one read. The client keeps one event to 256 KiB
     (`SSE_EVENT_MAX_BYTES`) and drops a larger one whole, never half parsed. A dropped connection reconnects with
     `Last-Event-ID` after a jittered backoff from 500 ms doubling to 30 s, from the upper half of each window, and
     gives up after 8 failures in a row with nothing received; a server `retry:` raises the backoff's floor (within
     the cap); a 429's `Retry-After` is honoured, clamped to 1 to 60 s; a 401 or an `end` event signs in again, after a
     backoff, at most once per 60 s over the stream's whole life (`RELOGIN_WINDOW_MS`), and a second one inside the
     window is the end, said in a sentence; 502, 503 and 504 back off; any other 4xx is final and not retried. A plain
     request that meets a 401 signs in once and retries once. A JSON body silent for the request timeout (15 s) is cut,
     and a stream silent for 45 s (`STREAM_IDLE_MS`, three of the console's 15 s pings) is cut and resumed. The SSE
     parser keeps a CR that ends a chunk (a CRLF split across two chunks is one line end), and ignores an id that is
     not printable ASCII or is longer than 1024 characters, since the id goes back as the `Last-Event-ID` header and
     node throws on a header with a control byte. A Set-Cookie whose Max-Age is zero or less, or whose Expires is past,
     clears the session cookie. A console refusal sentence is folded onto one line (`oneLine`: control characters to
     spaces, at most 1000 characters).
  4. **The fork is host-local.** `chat-fork.mjs` reads `PI_SESSIONS_DIR` on the operator's host, copies the canonical
     `current.jsonl` to `~/.pi-dispatch/chat/<key>/source-<ms>.jsonl` (source `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW`, its descriptor
     re-checked for the device and inode `planFork` judged; destination `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW`, 0600, in 0700
     directories) and runs `pi --fork <copy> --no-tools` in the operator's current directory. pi 1.2.0's `--fork`
     copies the file into its own sessions directory and records the source as `parentSession`; forking the COPY
     keeps every path pi writes or records outside the store. The key is re-derived from the record
     (`sessionKeyOfRecord`, `DES-SESSION-KEY-IS-DERIVED-NOT-INDEXED`); `/api/run` never carries it. Before the copy is
     opened in pi, a y/N names the bytes, says the transcript is unredacted and names the provider pi will actually
     use (`forkModelOf`): when pi's settings name a default provider AND model (`hostDefaultsOf`: `defaultProvider`
     and `defaultModel` from the agent dir's `settings.json` ONLY; the current folder's `.pi/settings.json` is never
     read, since these flags decide where the unredacted transcript goes and that folder may be a repository someone
     else wrote; pi 1.2.0 itself applies project settings only in a folder the operator trusted, and not reading them
     at all is the simpler rule and copies no trust store), both are passed to pi as `--provider` and `--model`, which pi never replaces with the session's;
     otherwise the prompt names the run's own model (`sessionModelOf`: the last `model_change` or assistant message,
     what pi 1.2.0's `getBranchSelection` restores), used if pi knows it and has a key for its provider, and pi's
     fallback otherwise, since this command cannot see pi's keys. No TTY (stdin) is a refusal BEFORE the copy, so the
     unredacted file is never written for a question that cannot be asked. `~/.pi-dispatch` and its chat
     folders must be owned by the operator (`ensurePrivateDir`: another user's, a link or a non-directory refused, and
     one with group or other bits made 0700). No `PI_CONSOLE_*` variable reaches pi or `pi --version` (`childEnv`):
     the token is this command's credential, and a forked agent with `--tools` can run commands. That stripping is
     hygiene, NOT a boundary: with `--tools` the forked agent reads whatever the operator's shell and files allow (forge
     tokens in the shell's environment, the deployment `.env`, `~/.ssh`), which is why tools are off by default.
     **Nothing unredacted stays in `~/.pi-dispatch/chat`**: the signal handlers go on before the copy (with no listener
     a signal takes its default action and kills the process mid-copy, leaving a partial file); the copy is removed on
     a no, on SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP from the copy's start until the answer (exit 130, 143, 129), and once pi exits,
     each time with `<key>/` when that leaves it empty (`rmdir`, which refuses a folder that holds anything); a SIGTERM
     or SIGHUP passed on to pi ends the command 143 or 129, whatever pi exits with, by when `pi --fork` has written its own copy (`SessionManager.forkFrom` writes
     it before the first prompt, pi 1.2.0); while pi runs, SIGTERM and SIGHUP are passed on to it and SIGINT is left to
     it, so this process outlives pi and cleans up. pi's own copy, as unredacted as the source, is the operator's to
     keep or delete, and the command says so.
  5. **The terminal is a hostile-text sink.** `scrubForTerminal` removes every C0 control but newline (a tab becomes
     four spaces, CR and CRLF a newline), DEL, every C1 control (a lone 0x9b is CSI on some terminals) and the bidi
     controls, the zero-width characters (U+200B to U+200D, U+2060, U+FEFF), the soft hyphen, the tag characters
     U+E0000 to U+E007F and the Hangul fillers and leading jamo (U+1100 to U+115F, U+3164, U+FFA0), which hide text
     or that pi-tui measures at a width the terminal does not draw, and clips an entry to 64 KiB; pi-tui's hyperlinks
     are turned off, so a markdown link prints its target beside its text. The worker has already redacted the text
     and escaped its controls; the client trusts neither. **Markdown is a parser with limits, so its input is bounded
     first** (`markdownPlan`): an assistant entry is drawn as markdown only when no line stacks more than 8 quote or
     list markers (`MARKDOWN_MAX_DEPTH`) and it holds at most 2000 emphasis or link delimiters
     (`MARKDOWN_MAX_DELIMITERS`), and its LaTeX is rendered only when braces nest at most 16 deep
     (`LATEX_MAX_BRACE_DEPTH`) and the entry holds at most 256 backslashes (`LATEX_MAX_COMMANDS`: LaTeX also recurses
     on brace-free commands, `\sqrt\sqrt...x` or `\frac a\frac a...`, which overflow at 1,600 to 2,000 commands in
     `$...$`, `$$...$$` and `\[...\]` alike, so a brace bound alone is not one); otherwise plain text, and a render that throws falls back to plain text for that entry
     alone (pi-tui 1.2.0's Markdown overflows the stack at a 55-deep quote and is quadratic in emphasis). **The
     terminal is given back** (`guardTerminal`): while a screen runs, an uncaught exception, an unhandled rejection,
     SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP leave the alternate screen, show the cursor and end raw mode before the process exits,
     since pi-tui renders from a timer and a throw there would leave the shell with no cursor and no echo.
  6. **`/dispatch chat` (part 2) is the panel's, on the panel's footing.** The pi extension's command
     (`admin/src/dispatch-chat.mjs`) resolves the run through `resolveRunChat`, the function `/api/run` itself answers
     with (factored out of `getRun` for this, so the route, the panel and the Chat panel's rule are one), over a
     read-only fleet reader, and dispatches on its `mode`: live opens the overlay on the active job's tail
     (`makeDashboard({ initialTail })`), reply plans, confirms and writes the console's `parked-answer` through the
     panel's audit chain, fork runs `chat-fork`'s `planFork` and `runFork` inside a `ctx.ui.custom` component that
     stops pi's TUI first and starts it in a `finally`. The panel reads Valkey directly, as every other view of it
     does: it runs on the deployment's host with the deployment's own credentials, so the console's reason for the
     CLI (no Valkey password on an operator's terminal elsewhere) does not apply. The argument classes are restated
     rather than imported from `chat-cli.mjs`, whose literal dynamic import of the pi-tui view a bundler follows; the
     key's shape is imported (`SESSION_KEY_PATTERN`), and a test builds the admin bundle in memory and requires
     `chat-fork` inlined and no pi-tui, `chat-view.mjs`, `chat-cli.mjs` or `console-client.mjs` (and a test holds the
     restated classes to `classifyChatTarget` on a shared table, with one URL limit). `runFork`'s process exit on a
     signal at the question is turned into a "no" by its `proc` seam, since inside pi it would end pi; given such a
     seam `runFork` returns the signal's exit code with the copy removed and the line said once, and the panel reports
     an interruption, not a return from the fork. **The handover is hostile to pi in three ways, each closed** (review
     round 1, `handOver`): `tui.stop()` leaves the terminal cooked, so (1) Ctrl+C is a SIGINT, which with no listener
     ends pi: a no-op listener is held from before `tui.stop()` to after `tui.start()`; (2) a line read of the y/N
     takes Ctrl+D on an empty line as the END of stdin, for good, leaving pi's keyboard dead after `tui.start()`: the
     y/N is read in raw mode (`terminalAsk`; Ctrl+D and Ctrl+C are a "no", the input ending or closing too), its mode
     restored and its listeners removed. It is a LINE, judged whole on Enter (yes only for a trimmed y or yes), not one
     key (review round 2): the one-key read answered on the first y anywhere, so "why?" forked, and a y typed into pi a
     moment before the question, still buffered, answered a question nobody had seen. So the input is drained (pi's own
     `drainInput(1000, 50)`: discarded until 50 ms of quiet, at most 1 s) before the question shows and again after the
     answer, so the rest of a fast-typed line reaches neither the fork nor pi's screen. Any ESC is a "no", never parsed:
     a bare Esc and an arrow key both start with it and a chunk boundary can split a sequence, so telling them apart
     needs pi-tui's timing parser, and echoing the bytes would paint junk; a mis-pressed arrow costs a re-run, never an
     unwanted fork. Rejected: ignoring escape sequences (a heuristic that guesses wrong on a split chunk). `handOver`
     runs unawaited inside `ui.custom`, so a throw in it would be an unhandled rejection that ends pi: `tui.stop()` and
     `tui.start()` are each tried on their own and said ("chat: failed (...)"; after a failed stop nothing is forked
     and no exit code is reported), and the call carries a `.catch` that settles the dialog once; (3) pi's own SIGTERM or SIGHUP handler can exit the
     process before `runFork`'s (added later) remove the unredacted copy: `runFork` hands the panel its synchronous
     removal (`registerCleanup`), which the panel prepends on SIGTERM and SIGHUP and adds on `exit`. Rejected: making
     `runFork` take the terminal itself (it is the CLI's too, where a line read and a process exit are right), and
     keeping the cooked read with an `end` handler (once stdin has ended no handler gets it back). The parked answer
     is signed with the reserved name `panel`, whose trail names the /dispatch panel; rather than reserve the word in
     `TOKEN_NAME_RE` (which would make an existing token file of that name fail to load), the planner refuses a
     console token named `panel` (`planParkedAnswer`'s `from`). A question's lines are shown behind `  | ` and capped
     at 40, so agent-written text cannot pass for one of the panel's own notices; and Esc from a tail whose job is no
     longer the ACTIVE row rests the cursor on no row with a note, so a `t` meant for the watched run never steers
     another.
- **The client's other facts**:
  - **Which console**: `--console`, else `PI_CONSOLE_URL` from the shell, else the deployment's `PI_CONSOLE_LISTEN`
    (`cliDeploymentEnv`: the shell's, else the folder's `.env`, a disagreement refused), else `127.0.0.1:4790`. A
    `PI_CONSOLE_LISTEN` read that way must be loopback (127.0.0.0/8, `::1`, `localhost`, a wildcard dialled on
    loopback) or a unix socket, or it is refused naming `--console` and `PI_CONSOLE_URL`: the folder's `.env` may be a
    repository someone else wrote. A value the shell does not set came from that file, and is taken only when the
    file passes the panel's rule (`dotenvTrustRefusal` over `readDeploymentEnv`: owned by this account or root, no
    group or other write on it or a folder above it) and is not a symbolic link (`lstat`); loopback alone is not
    enough, since another local account can listen on a loopback port and collect the token. Before signing in to any other address (only `--console` or `PI_CONSOLE_URL` can
    name one; a hostname is judged by its spelling, never resolved, `isLoopbackAddress`), the CLI warns that the token
    travels over plain HTTP to that host and asks y/N, default no; `--yes` answers it, and the warning still prints. An
    `https:` address is refused (the console speaks plain http on loopback, TLS is the tunnel's, and its origin check
    compares against `http://<Host>`, so a TLS client could read but never write); a wildcard listen (`0.0.0.0`,
    `[::]`) is dialled on its loopback twin.
  - **Which token**: `PI_CONSOLE_TOKEN` from the shell only, else a hidden prompt on a TTY. Never the deployment's
    `.env`: that file is the service's, readable by whoever runs the service, and a token in it would be an operator
    credential beside the worker's secrets.
  - **pi-tui is imported lazily** (`loadPiTui`), only when a screen is drawn, so the fork, the pure helpers and the
    worker's boot never load it. It is an exact pin of the worker (`@earendil-works/pi-tui`), held to the runner's pin
    by `pi-pin-check.mjs` and moved by `pi-bump.mjs`'s table (`CONST-PI-VERSION-PINNED`).
  - **After a live run ends** (its stream's `done`, or the poll's mode for a viewer), the CLI asks `/api/run` again up
    to 5 times, 2 s apart, until the mode leaves `live` (the record lands a moment after `done`), then goes on in the
    new mode: a park drops into the reply view, a finished run into the fork. A run still live after that is a
    refusal sentence, not a guess.
  - **Exit codes**: 0 after a detach, an answer, leaving without one and a declined fork; pi's own code for a fork
    (143 or 129 once a SIGTERM or SIGHUP was passed on to it);
    130, 143 or 129 for SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP at the fork's question or on a chat screen; 1 for a refusal.
  - **The URL lookup is an exact-target scan**: `readRunsPage`'s `match` predicate (`targetKeyOf`) is applied beside the
    kind filter, so `TARGET_RUNS_MAX` counts runs on THAT target over at most `RUNS_PAGE_EXAMINE_MAX` (2000) records
    examined, never the filter's substring `q`, which let `#120`, `#121`... fill the page and crowd out `#12`. A 404
    after a truncated scan says it searched the newest 2000 runs; a newer-run search that stopped before the record's
    own instant is unknown, never "no later run"; a page whose history or run mirror could not be read is unreadable
    (503 for a URL).
  - **Known limit**: a URL whose only run is still active answers 404 asking for the run id, because a running job has
    no record until it ends and the URL lookup reads the run history (`TARGET_RUNS_MAX`, one runs page).
- **Why**: the issue asked for three things a terminal can do with a run (read and continue a finished one, attach to
  a running one and steer it, answer a parked one) and, by decision, the same in the web console. Each of the writes
  already existed as a console action with its guards, ticket and audit, so going through the console adds no write
  path and no auth model; and an operator on another machine already has the SSH tunnel the browser uses. The fork is
  the one mode the console cannot serve without a route that hands out an unredacted transcript, so it runs where the
  transcript already is.
- **Rejected**:
  - **Writing the fork back to the canonical session.** The next job on that issue would resume from the operator's
    local chat, a second writer beside the worker's promotion with no lock between them, and text the operator typed
    would reach a job as if it were the run's own history. A fork is the operator's copy and stays theirs.
  - **`pi --session <current.jsonl>` in place.** pi appends to the file it opens, so this IS a write-back, by the
    back door. `--fork` on a private copy was chosen instead.
  - **A bearer header for the client.** A second way in, judged by code the browser path never runs, and every guard
    in `guards.mjs` (Host, Origin, the JSON type) would need a twin. The cookie from the same token login is the
    console's one model.
  - **A raw-transcript route on the console** (to fork from another machine). The stored transcript is unredacted
    (whatever a tool printed, a secret included); the console only ever serves the redacted live stream, and a route
    that served the store would make every operator token a key to every kept session. A remote fork is left to
    `OQ-046`'s redaction question.
  - **The CLI reading Valkey directly** (as `pi-dispatch steer` does). It would need the deployment's Valkey URL and
    password on the operator's terminal, bypass the console's roles, tickets and audit, and judge the mode on its own
    reads, free to disagree with the page.
  - **Tools on by default in a fork.** The conversation is text an agent wrote while reading untrusted input, and the
    fork runs in the operator's own folder, not the job's workspace or container: a forked agent with tools would act
    on the operator's machine on that text's say-so. `--tools` is an explicit opt-in.
  - **WebSockets** for the live view. The traffic is one way plus the existing two-step actions; SSE through the same
    dispatcher and guards already serves the page, and `DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE` rejected WebSockets for the same
    reasons.
  - **Resetting the re-login rule on any delivered entry** (review round 1). It let a server that delivers one entry
    and then `end`, forever, drive sign-ins without bound; the rule is now once per 60 s over the stream's whole life.
  - **Finding a pending answer by its keys** (review round 1). Its delivery id is fresh per answer and its semantic
    window names the comment trigger's flow and lapses after ten minutes; only a queue scan can say a run on the
    target is coming.
  - **A JSON stream for the browser too.** `DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE` rejected rendering in the browser so that one
    escaper serves every page; that stands. The JSON format exists because a terminal is not HTML and renders itself,
    and its own sink (`scrubForTerminal`) is the terminal's escaper.
  - **`/dispatch chat` through the console's HTTP API** (part 2), like the CLI. The panel already holds the
    deployment's Valkey and run history for every other view and writes through the same audit chain; a console
    round trip would add a token prompt and a running console as preconditions and buy nothing.
  - **`/dispatch chat` as a model-callable tool.** It queues a paid resume or hands the terminal to another program;
    like steering (`DES-ADMIN-VIA-PI-EXTENSION`), its sender must be the person at the keyboard. The tool enumeration
    is unchanged.
  - **A pi-tui chat screen inside the panel** for live and reply. The overlay already tails the live transcript and
    steers the ACTIVE row, and pi's own dialogs ask for an answer; a second renderer in the admin bundle would pull
    pi-tui's terminal view in and duplicate both.
- **Residuals**: the fork sends an unredacted transcript to the operator's own provider (decided: the y/N naming the
  provider and `--no-tools`; open: redacting the snapshot, `OQ-046`); a pull or merge request's run cannot be forked by
  its id (its key needs the head branch, which no record carries) and must be named by its key; an Azure work item in
  several repositories needs the run id (409 with candidates).
- **Traces to**: `REQ-TERMINAL-CHAT`, `REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY`, `REQ-OPERATOR-CONSOLE-SCREENS`, `REQ-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT`,
  `REQ-STEER-RUNNING-JOB`, `REQ-AWAIT-INPUT`, `DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`, `DES-SESSION-KEY-IS-DERIVED-NOT-INDEXED`,
  `DES-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`, `INT-CONSOLE-STATE-API`, `INT-CONSOLE-EVENT-STREAM`, `INT-SESSION-STORE-CONTRACT`,
  `CONST-PI-VERSION-PINNED`, `CONST-ISSUE-TEXT-IS-DATA`, `OQ-046`.
- **Code evidence**: worker/src/chat-mode.mjs (`chatModeOf`, `runStateOf`, `CHAT_REFUSALS`), worker/src/chat-cli.mjs
  (`classifyChatTarget`, `runChat`, `settle`), worker/src/chat-fork.mjs (`planFork`, `copySnapshot`, `runFork`,
  `resolvePiBinary`, `piVersionOf`, `hostDefaultsOf`, `sessionModelOf`, `forkModelOf`, `childEnv`, `ensurePrivateDir`),
  worker/src/chat-view.mjs (`scrubForTerminal`, `markdownPlan`, `guardTerminal`, `parseChatInput`,
  `editorAvailability`, `makeChatScreen`, `runLiveView`, `runReplyView`, `questionOf`, `loadPiTui`),
  worker/src/console-client.mjs (`parseConsoleAddress`, `consoleAddressOf`, `consoleToken`, `makeSseParser`,
  `backoffMs`, `retryAfterMs`, `makeConsoleClient`, `isLoopbackAddress`, `oneLine`), worker/src/session-key.mjs
  (`sessionKeyOfRecord`), worker/src/cli.mjs (the `chat` verb), admin/src/console/run-api.mjs (`chatFactsOf`,
  `NEWER_CACHE_MS`), admin/src/console/transcript.mjs (`transcriptEntryJson`, `TRANSCRIPT_FORMATS`),
  admin/src/console/live.mjs, admin/src/console/server.mjs, admin/src/console/pages.mjs (`loadPageData`),
  admin/src/console/panels.mjs (`runChat`, `parkedInbox`, `overviewParked`), admin/src/job-actions.mjs
  (`parkedAnswerRefusalOf`, `planParkedAnswer`), admin/src/read-model.mjs (`forgeTargetOf`, `readJobStatus`,

## DES-DOCTOR-RESULTS-PUBLISHED

- **Status**: issue #712, PR C (2026-10-21). New. The key's contract is `INT-DOCTOR-RESULTS-KEY`.
- **Decision**: every `pi-dispatch doctor` run publishes what it judged to Valkey, one record per host
  (`doctor:h:<host>`, kept 7 days from the last publish), and the worker runs `pi-dispatch doctor --publish` itself, as
  a child process, a minute after boot and then every `PI_DOCTOR_INTERVAL_HOURS` (24 by default, 0 = never, at most
  168). The console's Fleet page draws a Doctor panel from the records, the console's "does not load" sentences quote
  the matching check, and the `/dispatch` panel's HOSTS view gives each host its doctor lines.
  - **What is published**: each check's stable `id` and its level (ok, warn, fail), counts over every check, and for a
    warn or a fail only its label and fix, REDACTED: an absolute or home path becomes `<path>`, a URL keeps its scheme
    and host, every value of a secret-named variable doctor saw (this shell's and the deployment `.env`'s) and every
    known token shape becomes `[redacted]`, control characters become spaces, and each string is capped at 300
    characters. An ok check publishes its id and level only.
  - **Ids**: a check doctor's console sentences match on carries a NAMED id at its site (`triggers.file`,
    `settings.overlay`, `<boot file>.file` and `.file-shell`, `NAMED_CHECK_IDS`); every other check is
    `<section>.<n>`, its place in one of 33 pinned sections on that run (`DOCTOR_SECTIONS`, marked in `collectChecks`).
    A derived id is a key for a list, stable for one host's configuration and not across hosts; a test pins the
    sections and the named ids against the source, and a repeat is suffixed so no two entries share an id.
  - **Best effort**: a Valkey this run may not talk to (the owner rule, a database that does not exist, a line doctor
    cannot read) is not written to, a write that fails is one line on stderr, and neither changes what doctor prints on
    stdout or its exit code. `--no-publish` skips the write; `--publish` beside it is refused (exit 2).
  - **The worker's run**: the same CLI entry an operator types, without `--live`, `--secrets` or `--fix`, plus the
    internal `--by-worker=<hours>`, so the record says the worker ran it and carries the interval it really runs at;
    stdout is discarded and the TAIL of stderr read for the one "not published" prefix only; a run is killed after
    120 s, as a whole process group on POSIX (the child is spawned detached, so the kill reaches the `docker` calls and
    the canary probe it started; on Windows the plain kill); a tick while a run
    is in flight starts none; the timers are unref'd and the spawner is an `extraClosers` entry, which kills a run in
    flight on shutdown. It logs `doctor_published` (`code`, `signal`, `ms`, `published`) or `doctor_spawn_failed`
    (`reason`), integers and names only.
- **Why**: "run pi-dispatch doctor for the reason" sent an operator from the console to a shell on a host they may not
  have open, for a reason doctor already knew. A host nobody runs doctor on is exactly the one whose problems nobody
  has seen, so a publish only on the operator's runs would leave it empty; hence the worker's own run. Seven days is a
  week of daily runs with room for a weekend outage, and a result that outlives its host's runs by two intervals is
  flagged stale rather than trusted.
  - **Why redaction is stricter than the terminal's**: doctor's lines are written for the person at that host's
    keyboard; they name paths and print configured values. A record is read by every console viewer, from another
    machine, and the console shows a viewer only basenames (`DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`'s PATHS rule). Doctor already prints
    set or unset for the secret service keys and URLs through `urlShown`; the redaction is the second line, so a value
    that slipped into a label one day still does not leave the host.
  - **Why the console's labels are for both roles**: they are doctor's own sentences, after redaction, about the
    deployment's configuration, not run text (`REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY` (l) keeps `failedReason` and the transcript for
    operators because a forge payload or the agent shapes them; nothing an outsider writes reaches a doctor label).
  - **A display, not a decision**: nothing reads `doctor:*` to decide anything (not the worker, the receiver, or
    doctor). Deleting the keyspace while the fleet runs changes no host's behaviour, the registry's test
    (`INT-HOST-REGISTRY-CONTRACT`).
- **Rejected**:
  - **Running doctor in the worker's process** (importing `runDoctor`). Doctor is synchronous file reads, runtime
    spawns and its own Valkey clients; inside the worker its stalls would land on the event loop that renews BullMQ's
    job locks (`maxStalledCount: 0` fails a paid job whose lock lapses), and its faults would be the worker's. A child
    has its own loop, crash and kill, and judges exactly what an operator's run judges.
  - **Publishing the labels as doctor prints them.** They carry home paths, deployment layout and, through a parse
    error, file content; a console page is the place an operator screenshots. The redaction costs the path, which the
    operator has on the host anyway.
  - **No TTL** (keep the last result until the next). A host that was removed would then show its last problems
    forever, and the reader could not tell a host that stopped from one that is quiet; the expiry is what makes absence
    mean "no recent result".
  - **A HASH per host, the registry's shape.** A run is one snapshot that replaces the last one whole; `SET ... PX`
    writes it and its expiry in one command, with no window between them and no field left from a longer run.
  - **Publishing only on the operator's runs.** The decision (2026-10-21) was both: a hand run publishes, and the worker
    runs it daily, so a host nobody looks at is still described.
  - **Fix text only when it is a fixed sentence** (the plan's first wording). Telling a fixed sentence from an
    interpolated one at runtime would need a flag at each of the nearly five hundred sites that add a check; the fix goes through the same redaction as
    the label instead, which is what makes either safe.
- **Review round 1** (folded in before merge): a real run published JSON.parse's quote of a refused triggers file
  (`..."prompt": mysecretpr"...`), so the quoted input is cut to `<content>`; the path rule became a scanner that
  catches a path after any punctuation, a `~/`, an scp spelling and a path with spaces; the reader puts the live hosts
  before the index (seventy expired members had pushed a live host past the cap, and the panel said it never
  published) and the writer prunes too; a "does not load" sentence quotes THIS host's record first (each host has its
  own copy of the file) and quotes nothing where this host's run saw the file load; a run by hand records its uid and
  names the worker run it replaced, so a sudo run over the worker's is said, not hidden; a `PI_WORKER_NAME` the worker
  refuses is never a key. The claims are now what the rules guarantee, not "never a value".
- **Review round 2** (folded in before merge): invisible characters (zero-width, joiners, marks, the soft hyphen, the
  byte-order mark) are DELETED before every rule, since one inside a token or a path split it past recognition; the
  JSON.parse cut starts where Node's message starts, so a quoted value earlier in the label survives; credential query
  and fragment parameters by any name, `password=`/`password:`, `--password`/`--token`, `Basic <base64>` and `*-api-key:`
  headers lose their values; a numeric or switch value of a secret-sounding knob (`PI_DAILY_TOKEN_CAP=40`) is not taken
  as a secret; `--by-worker` outside 1 to 168 hours exits 2.
- **Residuals**: a secret under a variable whose name does not look like one, with no known token shape, written
  outside a URL and outside a credential-named assignment, is not recognised (doctor does not print such values
  today); a path written with fullwidth slashes, or relative (`./x`, `../x`, `Users/rob/x`), is kept; the user name of
  an scp spelling (`rob@host:<path>`) is kept; a doctor child the worker spawned is detached for the group kill, so it
  escapes a worker that crashes and runs to its own bounds (120 s at most is the worker's, doctor's own are shorter); a derived id moves when a check before it in its section is
  skipped, so the console matches on named ids only; the worker's run starts the egress canary's short-lived probe
  where the policy is armed, as every plain doctor run does.
- **Traces to**: `INT-DOCTOR-RESULTS-KEY`, `INT-HOST-REGISTRY-CONTRACT`, `DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`,
  `DES-RETENTION-SWEEPS-ON-A-TIMER` (the interval idiom), `REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY`, `REQ-OPERATOR-CONSOLE-SCREENS`,
  `REQ-DEPLOYMENT-BOOTSTRAP`.
- **Code evidence**: worker/src/doctor-results.mjs (`assignCheckIds`, `redactText`, `secretValuesIn`,
